544174|2026-03.headline: TBO Tek Q4 FY26 grew YoY on top and bottom line despite Middle East war; Q1 FY27 guided better than Q4 and last year, with no figures given.
544174|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 showed YoY growth in revenue and profit despite the war that began at end-February 2026, which hit the Middle East and Israel, TBO's largest source markets. January and February showed strong operating leverage, margin expansion and EBITDA growth YoY, but March was a washout and erased the quarter-level leverage. Management expects Q1 FY27 to beat Q4 and last year on both GTV and gross profit, while declining to quantify it. Cash flow from operations was negative in FY26, which management attributed mainly to timing items (Brazil anticipation discontinuation, war-related receivable delays, PLB payouts and deposits classified as working capital) and expects reversion to over 100% cash conversion by year-end.

financial_highlights.value: Rs. 110 crore (as cited by analyst; company did not dispute)
financial_highlights.change: Management did not give YoY figure on the call; growth stated only qualitatively
Expected to taper slightly in FY27

financial_highlights.value: ~4-5% YoY for full year, primarily hotel GTV
financial_highlights.change: Management does not report constant currency

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow and FCF FY26
financial_highlights.change: Management attributes to timing; FY25 CFO/PAT ~90% per analyst

segments.commentary: Hotel GTV is about 50:50 retail vs API by GTV, with retail higher on gross profit; hotels are higher-margin and expected to grow faster than air GTV. Hotel GTV carries most of the FX benefit.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: Air GTV is back to about Rs. 3,400 crore on an organic basis per analyst; management says Q1 air trajectory is a shade better than Q4.

segments.name: Classic Vacations / North America
segments.commentary: Management views Classic and TBO North America as one business; expects significant YoY growth but declined to quantify. Integration is about halfway; target completion by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: LATAM (Brazil)
segments.commentary: Management expects moderate growth in FY27 given currency and IOF tax headwinds; Brazil is not among top three source markets.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Growing from a small base, led by Australia after investment; some APAC-based API partners add growth. Price-competitive market.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 GTV and gross profit expected to grow YoY and QoQ, assuming no change in geopolitical status quo; no figures given.
Q1 FY27 EBITDA expected to grow in USD terms YoY and vs Q4; management declined to comment further.
SG&A growth to taper slightly from ~16%; top line to grow faster than SG&A, with operating leverage and margin expansion as the aim.
Long-term aspiration to grow early-to-mid 20s% per year; management says unless normalcy weakens, growth should stay in that range.
Cash flow conversion expected to return to over 100% of EBITDA/PAT by end of FY27, per management; timing items to resolve after Q2.
Brazil anticipation loss expected to fade after Q2 FY27 as receivables recover; ETR of 18% to 18.5%.
capex_capacity: Tech costs capitalised only for new features and products; amortisation period 3 to 5 years.
Classic platform migration underway; integration targeted to complete by end of calendar 2026.
Classic supply access: TBO connectivity established, but only high-curation luxury hotel supply opened to Classic so far.
Debt: five-year facility with one-year moratorium; repayments start Q3 FY27 and run four more years.
demand_pricing: Middle East and Israel saw sharp drops; management says Middle East bookings in April-May are slightly better than 30-40% below pre-war, but still well below normal in volume terms; in pockets volumes match pre-war levels.
Demand is shifting to Europe and Asia Pacific; Japan popular with HNIs, ultra-HNI still travelling to Europe.
Airfares higher and some airline capacity cut (domestic and international), though management views part of the cuts as temporary.
Take rate: management says no downward pressure currently, intends to hold current levels and not raise them.
Expedia: management says it is not a direct competitor in most of TBO's growth markets; B2B growing faster than B2C industry-wide.
Cancellations exceeded bookings for some pockets (Israel) during March; enterprise-level sales never negative for a day.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any reason for Q4's strong hotels and ancillary growth despite geopolitical shocks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to market-development investment starting January 2025, with new travel agents becoming productive after 6-9 months; some large partners went live in Q4. Majority of growth is market share gain.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA-to-GTV (stable at ~1% over three years) rise in FY27 as SG&A growth tapers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management considers it a reasonable assumption, driven by SG&A tapering and mix shift toward higher-margin hotels.

qa_highlights.question: How much EBITDA was lost in March due to the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; said costs were unchanged and incremental GTV would have largely flowed to the bottom line, a significant loss.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital drivers and when do cash flows normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were PLB payouts (Jan-Dec for hotels, April-March for air), delayed Middle East collections around Eid, bank deposits over 12 months classified in working capital, and Brazil anticipation reversal; expected to normalise by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How is management handling competitive pressure on take rates?
qa_highlights.answer: No downward pressure today; management intends to hold take rates at current levels and not raise them, as TBO operates an aggregation model.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rupee depreciation help GTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year YoY FX impact estimated at 4-5%, primarily on hotel GTV. Management will consider constant-currency reporting after an analyst suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SG&A plan for Classic and North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Early days; platform migration underway. Management will look at combined TBO North America and Classic cost base before commenting on dollar cost reduction.

risks_watch: Middle East and Israel recovery pace; management says two quarters of normalcy are needed before judging the growth reset.

Airline capacity cuts and higher airfares may reduce ticket volumes for the same GTV, especially in summer season (Q2).

544174|2026-06.headline: TBO TEK Q1 FY27: EBITDA-to-GTV of 1.3% and operating leverage shown despite Middle East disruption; 24% Europe growth, 15% organic CC growth.
544174|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) as the toughest in two years due to Middle East-driven travel disruption, yet reported top-line and bottom-line growth. Europe grew 24% YoY and Middle East was flat (1% CC growth), with Classic Vacations (acquired about six months ago) adding North America scale. EBITDA margins expanded faster than gross profit, which management cited as evidence of operating leverage. Management began reporting constant-currency numbers because a roughly 11% INR-vs-CC gap in hotel GTV distorted YoY growth. Management declined to give a timeline for Middle East normalisation or a long-term margin target.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 24% YoY in a weak quarter, helped by market development investments made last year; management says Europe and APAC lead growth.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Analyst cited about 15% growth in APAC alongside 30%+ Europe; management said APAC and Europe are leading the growth charter.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Flat, +1% in constant currency; inbound travel to Middle East is under serious stress, while TBO's outbound business is less exposed.

segments.name: North America (Classic Vacations)
segments.commentary: North America is nearly a quarter of hotel GTV after Classic acquisition; Classic has highest GP profile (about 11%) and is seasonally strongest in Q1 on check-in basis.

segments.name: Airlines
segments.commentary: Airline GTV grew about 15% YoY; airline GP profile is about 1%, so airline mix shifts take rate.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for both QoQ and YoY growth; Q2 expected to be somewhat better than Q1 given July is the heaviest northern hemisphere travel month.
Management expects SG&A growth to be significantly slower than GP growth, though SG&A growth may tick up in Q2 due to increment season and opportunistic market development.
Classic platform integration expected to finish by end of calendar 2026; Classic-to-TBO selling expected to start early next year after platform migration.
Management said margins should expand as top-line normalises, but gave no long-term margin target; said it is not anchoring to 45-60% steady-state platform margins.
Operating leverage expected to continue; Q2 expected to show some margin expansion, Q3 historically lower revenue and margin dip.
Full-year Classic EBITDA margin of about 2.5% described as a fair assessment by management.

Platform integration (TBO and Classic) expected to be completed by calendar year end 2026.
VOYA AI itinerary tool is experimental; capex minimal and capitalised as intangibles; built in-house by tech team.
AI-based CRM layer launched a few weeks before the call; too early for results.
demand_pricing: Middle East situation described as extremely fluid; management declined to forecast when Middle East returns to growth.
Take rate slightly lower in Q1 as regions fought for business in the crisis; management accepted lower margins to win share.
Airfares very high; Middle East carriers disruption hit East-West travel, affecting India and Europe.
Management claims share gains in APAC and Europe, citing high double-digit growth in a market with no organic growth.
GTV split between retail and B2B/API roughly 50-50, unchanged from last quarter; management will review disclosure.
Management expects bigger players to gain share as smaller and mid-sized players attrite post crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1.3% consolidated EBITDA-to-GTV sustainable and can it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA-to-GTV is tricky due to airline vs hotel take-rate differences; the right metric is EBITDA-to-GP, at about 26%, which should keep improving.

qa_highlights.question: How should organic growth be modelled once conditions normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a return to the growth profile of Q3 FY26, timing uncertain (Q3 or Q4); Europe and APAC lead, with North America growth expected from October-December on a like-for-like basis.

qa_highlights.question: How will Classic's December-quarter consolidation affect GP growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two opposing forces exist: Classic has not yet delivered standalone enterprise growth (a few quarters away), while pre-war organic growth in Jan-Feb was above 15%.

qa_highlights.question: How long can APAC and Europe growth last before the next investment cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: A key account manager typically shows four to six quarters of growth; no early signs of slowdown, with investments expected to be sticky.

qa_highlights.question: Is the SG&A run-rate of about 4% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A growth may expand a little in the short term due to increment season and market development, but will be range-bound and slower than top line.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 30 bps drop in organic hotels GP/GTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split the drop between lower Middle East saliency and deliberate margin cuts to protect volumes, saying both occurred.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and cross-sell status?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash in bank Rs. 1,980+ crore against USD 70 million loan and EUR 6 million working capital loan; about INR 65 crore of TBO-to-Classic sales, reverse flow not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11% currency impact due to a policy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no policy change; the gap is purely rupee depreciation, and CC reporting will continue directionally.

Strong per analyst; management says tricky metric to track

risks_watch: Middle East escalation: management says the situation changes hourly and it will not forecast when the region returns to growth; inbound Middle East businesses under serious stress, with possible attrition if it persists.

Classic Vacations: standalone enterprise growth is a few quarters away, and the December-quarter consolidation will blend in a seasonally uneven base; platform migration (expected by calendar year-end 2026) and reverse cross-sell (expected early next year) are not yet started.
Currency: about 11% INR-vs-CC gap in hotel GTV this quarter versus about 3% previously; management says there was no policy change, and CC reporting is promised directionally in future quarters.

Margin sustainability: take rate was slightly lower in Q1 as regions competed for share; management said it will selectively drop margin to win business, and the 30 bps fall in organic hotels GP/GTV was not split between saliency and deliberate price cuts.

Investment cycle: management says market development spend may rise opportunistically and SG&A growth may tick up in Q2 with increment season; sustainability of Europe and APAC growth beyond four to six quarters is uncertain.
Disclosure: the retail vs B2B/API GTV split is roughly 50-50, and management only said it will review what disclosure it can provide on the API business, which an analyst flagged as a key driver.

I would really not hazard a guess on what is going to happen in the Middle East and when it comes back to growth.
Those are the two opposing forces that we need to blend for. I don't have an answer for you that what will that blend will look like.

For us it just becomes very hard to model by looking at GTV as blended GTV, but what we do know is and from at this point SG&A is unless we choose to and we will tell you if we choose to re-look at accelerating market development etc., our SG&A growth will be significantly slower than GP growth and hence those margins should expand meaningfully.

544176|2026-03.headline: Aadhar Housing Q4 FY26: AUM crossed INR30,571 crore (+20% YoY), FY26 PAT INR1,096 crore (+20%), GNPA eased to 1.08%.
544176|2026-03.overview: Aadhar closed FY26 with AUM of INR30,571 crore, up 20% YoY, and record Q4 disbursements of INR3,087 crore (+20% YoY). FY26 disbursements were INR9,556 crore (+17%) and PAT was INR1,096 crore (+20%), or INR1,108 crore before the one-time Labour Code charge. GNPA was 1.08%, down 30 bps QoQ but up slightly from 1.05% a year earlier, with 1+ DPD improving 78-80 bps QoQ. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with spreads expected to contract 8-10 bps.

financial_highlights.change: -30 bps QoQ; vs 1.05% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Exit cost of funds / exit spread

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; home loan disbursements grew about 26% YoY in Q4, helped by PMAY subsidies (about INR50 crore to about 15,000-16,000 customers) and a push on emerging markets.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP / non-housing)
segments.commentary: 27% of AUM; LAP disbursement mix was about 24-25% in Q4 versus 28-29% typical, deliberately held back since the tariff shock. Management is open to lifting it to 27-28% of disbursements, but not in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Emerging and urban geographies
segments.commentary: Average ticket about INR10.9 lakh on the book. Emerging C is about INR8.5-8.6 lakh, emerging B INR10 lakh, emerging A INR12 lakh, urban INR17-18 lakh. Urban traction is 'encouraging' per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth, and 17-18% disbursement growth.
Spreads expected to contract by about 8-10 bps YoY, given incremental yields of about 13% against a book yield of about 13.52%; partly offset by LAP mix and self-employed shift.
Cost-to-income ratio expected to fall by about 50 bps in FY27, driven by productivity and AI-led sales tools.
Cost of funds expected to hold broadly flat for the next 2-3 quarters; management would be 'very happy' to hold the 7.7% exit rate through FY27.
Direct assignment (DA) volume expected to grow 10-15% in FY27 from about INR1,725 crore in FY26.
Long-term AUM milestone of INR50,000 crore targeted in about 3 years.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 626 across 22 states and more than 550 districts, after 5 branches added in Q4 and 46 in FY26.
Four branch categories: ultra micro (50-60 sq ft), micro, small and main. Small branches take 9-12 months to turn productive and urban branches 12-15 months.
Undrawn sanctions of INR1,687 crore, of which INR246 crore from NHB.
Liquidity of INR1,425 crore at end-Q4 FY26.
Employees: on-roll about 5,400-5,430 and off-roll about 3,900-3,965 at March 2026, versus 4,600 on-roll and 4,300 off-roll a year earlier.
Management expects Uttar Pradesh to be the largest contributor to growth; West Bengal flagged as a potential new state.
demand_pricing: Demand described as end-user driven, with first-time homebuyers prominent. Competition from banks is elevated in urban markets but steady in low-income segments.
Management cited state-level BLC and AHP pipelines (for example, 25,000+ units in Odisha) as supporting demand.
Bounce rates stable for six quarters and unaffected by West Asia conflict; collections team of about 2,000 briefed to be careful.
Low-income segment: management says about 18% share of the low-income HFC peer group, up from 16-17%.
Borrowing mix at March 2026: banks 51%, NHB 22%, NCD 19%, ECB 5%, others 4%. 76% of borrowings are floating; 73-74% of assets are floating.
NCDs are 22% of borrowings, of which 68% are fixed. NHB funding is roughly 50% fixed and 50% floating.

qa_highlights.question: Why has LAP growth lagged, and what is the outlook for other income and ESOP cost?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP slowdown was deliberate since the tariff shock; LAP is 27% of AUM and LAP mix in Q4 was about 26%. Assignment income reflected spreads 80-85 bps better, not larger volumes. About INR6-7 crore of Q4 fee income was one-time. ESOP charge of INR13.5 crore is a Q4 item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for yields and spreads in FY27 given the rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a 2-3 quarter rate hold. Spread contraction of 8-10 bps is guided at the current 25-26% LAP mix. Each 5 percentage points shifted from HL to LAP adds about 400 bps on that portion.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 1+ DPD improvement and the sequential jump in disbursements?
qa_highlights.answer: 1+ DPD fell about 80 bps (not risen, as the analyst framed it) over 18 months of focus on collections. Sequential disbursement strength came from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Delhi, Karnataka and Uttarakhand. Incremental borrowing cost rose about 10 bps QoQ because bank drawdowns were deferred into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex-to-AUM rise sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 always carries sales contests and one-time incentive costs. Cost-to-income improved YoY from 37.9% to 37.1% in Q4. Full-year cost-to-income was 35.9%, down from 36.4%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ticket size trends and the sources of the home loan growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental ticket size ranged INR12.5-13.5 lakh over recent quarters, against INR10.9 lakh on book. Management aims to hold book ticket size at INR10-11.5 lakh, and to hold non-home loans to about 70:30 with home loans over the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the funding book can still reprice, and how far has cost of funds fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost fell from 8.4% to 7.6% YoY, with banks passing on 70-75 bps. Exit cost of funds moved from 8.14% to 7.72%, with 15 bps passed to customers. NCDs (22%) are mostly fixed, so the remaining repricing is limited to bank and floating NHB funds.

risks_watch: Geopolitical (West Asia) stress on borrowers; bounce rates and collections are the early indicators to watch.
Spread compression of 8-10 bps YoY if LAP mix stays at about 25-26%; cost of funds could rise given the 76% floating-rate liability book.
Competitive pressure from banks in urban markets.
Ticket size drift: management targets INR10-11.5 lakh, with construction-cost inflation expected to push it higher.
LAP usage is a lever to protect yields but is deferred; delinquency on LAP is about 0.7-0.75% higher on GNPA and must be watched when mix is raised.
Labour Code exceptional charge of INR16 crore taken in Q3; ESOP cost of INR13.5 crore in Q4 is a one-time item per management.

Our view is that the interest rate cycle has stagnated and to a certain extent, will be stagnant for at least two, three quarters.

544176|2026-06.headline: Aadhar Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 19% YoY to INR282 crores on AUM of INR31,364 crores (+18%), with disbursements hit by a switch to cheque-clearance recognition.
544176|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR31,364 crores, up 18% YoY, and exit spread held at 5.8% despite a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026. Disbursement was INR2,036 crores on the new cheque-clearance basis, against INR2,359 crores (+19% YoY) on the old cheque-handover basis, as the company moved recognition to clearance from Q1 FY27. Asset quality was stable YoY, with GNPA at 1.31% (down 3 bps) and Stage 2 at 3.3% (down 40 bps), though Q1 credit cost rose seasonally. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with the next three quarters targeted above 20%.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; non-home loans 27%. Incremental disbursement mix currently 76:24 home vs non-home, versus a historical 70:30.

segments.name: Non-home loans
segments.commentary: Disbursement growth slowed to about 22% in the quarter by the analyst's read; management called the slowdown a deliberate choice linked to the West Asia situation and the riskier profile of these loans.

segments.name: Emerging vs urban branches
segments.commentary: About 450 of 628 branches are in emerging locations. Emerging yields are 14-14.8% versus 11.5-12% in urban; average ticket size rose only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance held: 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth, 17-18% disbursement growth for the full year.
Disbursement growth above 20% targeted for each of the next three quarters; management expects Q2 to close the Q1 shortfall, with Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more.
July 2026 disbursement close to INR900 crores, per management.
Spread floor of 5.5% reiterated; over 2-3 years spreads expected to end near 5.5%, ROA 4.3-4.4% steady state, and ROE around 17% in a couple of years.
Cost-to-income expected to fall 30-40 bps a year; cost-to-AUM about 6-7 bps a year.
Credit cost expected to settle at 23-25 bps for the full year, with GNPA targeted at about 1.1% at year end.
Branch openings of 45-50 planned for Q3; Q1 had only 2 openings versus a 40-50 annual pace.
capex_capacity: Network at 628 branches across 22 states and 550+ districts as of June 2026.
New branches target productivity within 9-15 months; Q1 opened only 2 branches, with 5-7 planned and pushed into July.
Capital adequacy of 42.9% Tier 1 gives room for growth; the IPO's INR1,000 crores primary raise is meant to fund growth for the next 3-4 years. No plan to return capital.
Operational-risk capital set aside at about 6-7% of capital; balance-sheet risk weight about 45%.
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy and end-user, first-time-buyer driven, particularly in emerging markets; management reports no demand-side issues in urban locations.
Spreads held at 5.8% after a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026; management says it protects spreads over chasing yields.
Management expects 5-7% overlap with new affordable-segment entrants; Aadhar sits one notch below in low-income housing.
Incremental yields flat QoQ; management expects no decline if the urban/emerging mix moves toward 50:50.
NRI-linked exposure described as minimal; state-level rule caps any state at 15% of AUM, incremental disbursement or distribution.
Delhi's share rose slightly, a lower-yield state, yet yields held.

financial_highlights.change: includes ~INR14 crores quarterly ESOP cost; ~33-34% excluding it

qa_highlights.question: How is the company sustaining asset yields despite the 15 bps RPLR cut and competition, and is it due to pricing, mix, or segment changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited the urban/emerging strategy (about 450 of 628 branches in emerging locations) and a ticket size that moved only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh. Delhi's share rose slightly though it is a lower-yield state, and yields still held. No major state-mix shift was reported.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to sustain 20% growth and the 5.5% spread floor amid new affordable-segment entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Book spread is about 5.8%. Management expects a 5-7% overlap with new entrants, since Aadhar sits one notch below them in low-income housing, and says the emerging tilt will keep spreads above 5.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the July disbursement number and how will the cheque-clearance change be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: July disbursement is close to INR900 crores. Management expects Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more, with Q2 substantially covering the Q1 shortfall as the carry-forward business is recognised over a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cheque-clearance change affecting interest income, and what drove the sequential employee cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest income is affected by only 2-3 days, which management called immaterial. Sequential employee cost rose on the annual increment of about 10-12%. Year-on-year, the 27% rise is mainly INR14-15 crores of quarterly ESOP cost; excluding it, employee cost growth is about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 rise in GNPA and Stage 2 seasonal, and what is the full-year credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 credit cost is seasonally high at 40-45 bps for the last 2-3 years. Management expects the year to end with credit cost of 23-25 bps and GNPA near 1.1%. Q1 rose 25 bps versus a usual 30-35 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the liquidity buffer and cost-of-funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquidity was INR2,371 crores at quarter end, above 10% of borrowings, but management targets 7-8% intra-quarter and this rises at quarter end from drawdowns. Cost of funds moved little in Q1. Management sees no near-term impact from rate rises and says 75% of assets can be repriced.

risks_watch: Disbursement and PAT growth depend on Q2 catching up on the cheque-clearance shortfall; management targets Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more and above 20% for the next three quarters.
Non-home loan disbursement growth slowed to about 22%, and the home/non-home mix stood at 76:24 against a historical 70:30; management expects normalisation from Q3 once West Asia uncertainty eases.
Credit cost and GNPA: Q1 credit cost rose seasonally by 25 bps; the year-end GNPA target of about 1.1% and credit cost of 23-25 bps must hold.
Competitive pressure from affordable-segment entrants with a 5-7% overlap; spread floor of 5.5% and incremental yields flat QoQ.
Branch expansion slowed to 2 openings in Q1 against a 40-50 annual pace; 45-50 openings are planned for Q3 and 5-7 were pushed into July.
Cost of funds and interest-rate risk, with management expecting no imminent pass-through in the current or next quarter.
Monsoon and West Asia-related stress on rural and semi-urban cash flows, and NRI-linked exposure, which management called minimal.
key_quotes: Effective quarter 1, we have taken a step of transitioning our loan accounting to cheque clearance basis model of disbursement recognition, which is a forward -looking approach and a significant milestone in our commitment to governa nce, transparency and putting customer at the forefront.

Our approach, as always, has been to protect spreads rather than c hase yields, which we are doing by tilting the mix towards emerging branches by staying disciplined on loan against property and by continuing to drive productivity per branch and per employee, so that operating leverage does the work that pricing cannot.
And as we look at the current quarter and the upcoming quarter, which is quarter 3, we stand by our numbers of 45 to 50 branches.
So, I think Q2 itself, you will compensate the loss which we saw in Q1.

544177|2026-03.headline: Aztec H2 FY26 revenue up 12.4% YoY to ₹47.61 cr; FY26 revenue up 9.2% to ₹96.53 cr with EBITDA margin at 14.3%.
544177|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹96.53 cr (+9.2% YoY) and H2 revenue of ₹47.61 cr (+12.4% YoY). EBITDA rose 9.6% to ₹13.96 cr, with margin at 14.3% versus 14% a year earlier, while PAT was ₹7.41 cr, held back by higher depreciation, write-offs (up 85%), lower other income and tax. Management said the growth was below the earlier double-digit guidance and that it will prioritise margins over top-line growth. Capex is planned across infrastructure, exports and technology, but the absolute amount has not been disclosed and funding (internal accruals, debt, possibly equity) is still under evaluation.

financial_highlights.change: Impacted by higher depreciation, write-offs (+85% YoY) and lower other income
Tech infrastructure, systems, manufacturing, digital platforms

segments.name: Jettings (acquired subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹19.22 cr (+7%); EBITDA up over 18%. Employee cost down 20% and operating expenses down 11%, while purchases rose 41.5% to about ₹9 cr. Interest cost is the remaining weak point due to working capital intensity.

segments.name: Consumables (inks, wash, makeup/cleaner fluids)
segments.commentary: Management said makeup and cleaner fluids grew about 15% YoY and inks about 12.5% YoY in selling volumes. Ink and solvent mix is expected to shift as ink formulation is modified to reduce solvent consumption.

segments.name: Printers (CIJ, TIJ, DOD, laser, TTO, PIJ)
segments.commentary: An installed base of 8,000+ printers was cited, with 1,550 printers sold in FY26 per the call; the group-level tally was not reconciled on the call. Extrusion accounts for the largest share of CIJ applications (about 85%), and CIJ is said to make up ~95% across extrusion, food and FMCG.

segments.name: Government tenders and automation projects
segments.commentary: Two government tenders were won last year and more are in the pipeline. Management says project business is multi-month, high-ticket and built around a separate North and South team.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated sustainable double-digit medium-term growth but did not give a near-term number, and said margins take priority over top-line growth.
Management said it expects to hold the current EBITDA margin (about 13-14%) in FY27 and does not plan to chase top-line growth at the expense of margins.

Capex is split broadly as 41% infrastructure capacity, 30% exports and global expansion, 8% tech and ERP, 3% R&D and 5% product development and other initiatives. The absolute amount is still under board consideration.
Management said the full-year effect of recent investments will show up in FY27, and free cash flow is expected to rise with that.
capex_capacity: Capex is planned over the coming period across infrastructure capacity (41%), exports and global expansion (30%), tech and ERP (8%), R&D (3%) and other product development (5%). The absolute rupee amount has not been disclosed.
Funding is planned through internal accruals and debt, which management said have high visibility; equity remains under evaluation.
Backward integration: inks, wash and solvents are about 100% in-house; about 95% of the ink portion is integrated. Printer spares are 40-50% indigenised, with more in beta testing.
The Jettings integration progressed through the year-end and is contributing to operational synergies.
Management said the capex was deferred because of Middle East conflict visibility, and it was not committing advances until the outlook clears.
demand_pricing: Management said extrusion (PVC/CPVC pipes and wires) slowed in FY26 due to Middle East conflict effects on input costs, while FMCG and food did not see substantial slowdown.
Customer mix: extrusion is the largest vertical; others include food/pharma/FMCG, industrial equipment and automation, agriculture, packaging and printing, and 'others' at about 16.6% of top line.

Pricing: management said the company passes input cost increases on through service-linked AMCs, and that customers negotiate but ultimately accept. Inventory was built only to the extent customers could absorb, and the company declined to stock up at war-peak prices.
After-sales economics: management cited ₹80,000-1,20,000 per printer per year for extrusion customers (about ₹60,000 for some pharma and FMCG accounts), roughly equal to the printer cost per year.
Competition: management cited a fully integrated ink-to-printer model, backward integration and import-duty advantage over MNCs with overseas manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Installed base of 8,000+ printers versus 1,550 sold in FY26 does not reconcile with the prior 5,000+ base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the installed base includes Jettings-led sales and after-sales, and that the group-level number is correct. It was not broken down by company.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook: why should double-digit growth return after the 9.2% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Devraj Pandya said growth is the result of recent investments flowing into revenue over time, and that margins will be protected even if top-line guidance is missed. He cited diversification beyond extrusion as a hedge.

qa_highlights.question: Jettings acquisition: benefits achieved and performance versus plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jettings' revenue rose 7% to ₹19.22 cr and EBITDA margin rose to 10.2%, with lower employee and operating costs. It said the interest cost is still high because of working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: Government tenders and automation: size and timing of contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two tenders were won last year with more in the pipeline and that project business is multi-month, with a separate North and South team. The revenue size was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Capex amount and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the absolute capex is under board consideration and that broad percentage allocations are set. Funding is planned through internal accruals and debt; equity is still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Iran/Middle East conflict on raw material prices and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory was built only to customers' absorption capacity, and that service-linked AMCs make it easier to pass through costs. It expects the disruption to ease but said post-ceasefire effects can last 3-5 months.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 9.2% fell short of the earlier double-digit framework, and PAT growth was held back by depreciation, write-offs and tax.
Supply chain: heavy reliance on imported printheads and electronic components; management acknowledged this and cited a Taiwan Strait scenario as a risk.
Equity dilution: management said equity is still under consideration, while an analyst argued against it given the market capitalisation of about ₹123 cr versus reserves of about ₹44 cr.
Jettings working capital intensity and high interest cost.
Middle East conflict effects on raw material cost, CPVC/PVC demand and extrusion customer spending.
Customer concentration in extrusion; management is building vertical heads for FMCG/pharma, agriculture and extrusion.

544179|2026-03.headline: Go Digit reports 17.7% post-tax ROE on Indian Accounting Standards basis for FY26 and a 105.7% combined ratio, with GDPI up 16.2%.
544179|2026-03.overview: Management presented FY26 results re-based to Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS, effective 1 April 2026), which were audited for the first time, while stressing its internal KPIs remain NEP-based combined ratio plus DAC and IGAAP solvency. Full-year profit before tax on Ind AS plus DAC was INR239 crores in Q4 (vs INR142 crores) and post-tax profit was INR179 crores (vs INR106 crores). Q4 GDPI grew 21.3% and full-year GDPI grew 16.2%, while Q4 GWP growth slowed to about 6.2% because of a health reinsurance non-renewal. Solvency improved to 2.42 and AUM reached about INR23,000 crores (up 16.3%). Management said it sees motor pricing correcting in April and expects a regulatory response on expense of management (EOM) within 2-3 months.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Private car 44%, two-wheeler 32%, commercial vehicles 24% of business. OD/TP mix 38/62 vs industry 41/59. Own-damage loss ratio rose YoY; corrective action started, with impact expected from July-September quarter.

segments.name: Health (incl. group)
segments.commentary: Q4 health reinsurance non-renewal cost about INR252 crores (about INR200 crores in Q3). Retail is under 7% of health; employer-employee about 73% and non-employer-employee about 22%. Health market share about 1.3-1.4%.

segments.name: Fire / commercial
segments.commentary: Fire gross loss ratio 51% in FY26 vs 48% in FY25; net loss ratio rose on two large claims (INR55 crores gross in Q4). Cat treaty retention raised from INR36 crores to INR45 crores; earthquake limit raised from INR1,600 crores to INR2,000 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: Q4 two-wheeler premium was INR556 crores vs INR365 crores a year earlier, which pushed up EOM by about 3.5% in the quarter. Management estimates about 40% of FY26 two-wheeler business was new business.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Management plans to bid directly in government crop tenders this year, having previously written crop mainly through reinsurance acceptance; scheme structure not yet announced.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no numerical guidance; it said ROE and profitability are the focus.
Motor OD loss ratio expected to stabilise in July-September 2026 quarter and then fall; motor overall loss ratio targeted not to rise YoY in FY27.
New specialty commercial lines expected to reach about INR1,000 crores premium over 3-5 years.
Equity allocation at 8.5% of AUM with a 12.5% ceiling considered comfortable; fixed income duration at 4.5 years, with room to extend if rates rise.
Management expects EOM-related regulation within 2-3 months and expects the commission/management-expense split to be fixed.
Next year's effective tax rate expected at 25.2%.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance renewed for FY27: fire and other treaty capacity increased; property and engineering capacity raised with better commission terms.
A new miscellaneous treaty covers new risk types; an 11% quota share on non-motor, non-health premium was added to cap accumulation in Gujarat, Maharashtra and NCR.
Net retention for scooters and school buses was lowered through funds-withheld reinsurance after the Kolkata incident; management said this does not affect AUM.
Leverage rose to 5% (4.65% in June 2024); management expects it to hold around 5% over the next two years.
demand_pricing: Motor: management sees April 2026 price and commission correction in the market, and believes the market cannot sustain current prices. Growth outlook depends on the new-vehicle cycle, which was strong in H2 FY25.
Fire: softer terms seen in fire, but not in engineering, where growth was higher than fire. Fire market share about 3.9% on GWP.
Health: management plans to grow group health only if pricing improves by about 5%, and expects growth of 50-60% if loss ratio also falls by about 2%.
TP pricing: no motor TP hike this year; management said it is not privy to regulator thinking.
Competition: new non-life entrants are coming; management said it is not losing sleep over them and that EOM relief for new insurers should be split between commission and management expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Will fire profitability fall given higher cat reinsurance cost, net loss ratio deterioration, and a possibly softer fire market? Also, what is the crop strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with fire profitability, citing better commission in fire and engineering and profit commission on earned premium. Crop: will bid directly in tenders this year, pending government scheme structure.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fairfax keep its stake after the reverse merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not spoken to Fairfax and said there is no news on the amalgamation timeline. Fairfax holds about 58%; going below 51% would trigger an open offer, and management does not expect a sale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the new specialty commercial lines and what is the motor pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lines could reach about INR1,000 crores of premium in 3-5 years. Motor market correction in April 2026 on price and commission; overall motor loss ratio to be held flat or lower YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did motor OD loss ratio rise and what is the retention and renewal data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management delayed corrective OD pricing to test retention and sold more SAOD in FY25. Motor retention fell to 89.6% from 95.9%. Renewal rates rose in private car across channels.

qa_highlights.question: How will EOM compliance be managed at company level and how does Indian acquisition cost compare internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said line-of-business mix explains the EOM gap and expects regulation to ease expense limits within 2-3 months. Management said Indian acquisition costs have risen over 20 years and cited RBI and Economic Survey commentary.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the discounting benefit and will long-run Ind AS investment yield match IGAAP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount-rate effect is stable unless rates move sharply; it moved to 7.09% from 6.9%. Management said investment decisions should be judged on ROE, not on mark-to-market, and that risk-based capital may favour companies with high equity allocation.

risks_watch: Own-damage motor loss ratio: corrective action is due to show from July-September 2026; the next two quarters are the test.
Motor retention fell to 89.6% from 95.9%; watch renewal rates and whether the market price correction affects volume.
Fire net loss ratio: two large claims lifted net loss ratio; the cat reinsurance cost rise may compress margins.
EOM regulation: timing and form of relief are unclear, and new entrants may bring forbearance on EOM.
Health: non-renewal of a reinsurance treaty cut Q4 GWP growth to 6.2%; health loss ratios remain a question.

Ind AS vs IGAAP comparability: the DAC unwind (about 65% of INR2,470 crores in FY26-27), the 25.2% tax rate, and the non-booking of INR303 crores of unearned premium (INR109 crores acquisition cost provided) will affect reported profit.
Fixed income duration and rates: duration is 4.5 years; an interest rate move could affect unrealised losses (INR99 crores at 31 March 2026).

Am I losing sleep because of new competition? Not really.
And if you feel that our loss ratio would be worse than anyone else in the market, we'll be more than happy to learn and put more pressure on our management team, including Jasleen to improve.

rows.why: FY26 GDPI grew 16.2% vs industry about 13%, but Q4 GWP growth slowed to 6.2% (about 18.8% ex health reinsurance non-renewal), motor retention fell to 89.6% from 95.9%, and group health growth depends on about 5% pricing improvement.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Leverage rose to 5% (from 4.65% in June 2024) and management expects it to hold around 5% for two years; solvency is 2.42 and no physical capacity build-out was discussed, though reinsurance capacity was expanded for FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numerical guidance; only a motor loss ratio not rising YoY in FY27 and a specialty line target of about INR1,000 crores in 3-5 years, with no raise signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Motor OD loss ratio is still rising and corrective action only shows from July-September 2026, health reinsurance non-renewal cost about INR252 crores in Q4, and 65% of INR2,470 crores accumulated DAC unwinds in FY26-27, which will weigh on reported Ind AS profit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management targets a new specialty commercial lines book of about INR1,000 crores premium over 3-5 years, but no launch date or size for the next 2-4 quarters was given.

rows.label: EOM regulatory relief within 2-3 months
rows.why: Management expects regulation to fix the commission/management-expense split within 2-3 months; two-wheeler premium of INR556 crores vs INR365 crores pushed EOM up about 3.5% in Q4, so relief could ease expense ratio.

rows.label: Motor price and commission correction from April 2026
rows.why: Management sees the market correcting on price and commission and says it cannot be sustained, but no TP hike this year and timing is not confirmed, with motor retention at 89.6% vs 95.9%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Ind AS ROE of 17.7%, the combined ratio improvement and solvency of 2.42, but evasive on Fairfax, motor pricing timing and specialty-line sizing; analysts pushed on motor OD loss ratio, retention drop and fire net loss ratio.

544179|2026-06.headline: Go Digit's Q1 FY27 GDPI fell 8% and loss ratio rose to 73.3%, with management choosing profitability over growth.
544179|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a deliberately soft quarter, with gross written premium down 8% (about -2% excluding inward reinsurance in group health and crop). Motor own damage, mainly private car, drove the loss ratio up from 70.3% to 73.3%, and management said it had made the wrong call on the stand-alone OD renewals. On its internal KPI basis (NEP with DAC, excluding MTM and discounting), PAT was INR190 crore versus INR200 crore a year ago and combined ratio was 107.2%. Under Indian Accounting Standards (IFRS-style prescribed format), PAT rose to INR372 crore from INR325 crore, helped by unrealised gains and discounting.

financial_highlights.change: About -2% excluding inward reinsurance exits in group health and crop

financial_highlights.metric: PAT (internal KPI basis, DAC, excl. MTM and discounting)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR200 crore a year ago, -5%
vs INR325 crore in the prior-year quarter
from about INR4,600 crore at March 2026
from about INR7,600 crore at March 31, 2026
INR124 crore to INR187 crore total unrealised gains cited in IFRS results
Motor INR2,879 crore, non-motor INR508 crore
vs INR433 crore, +26% new business growth in 2W

segments.name: Motor own damage (private car)
segments.commentary: Primary driver of the loss ratio increase; management cut stand-alone OD and non-new car business, with stabilisation expected in Q2 FY27. Motor overall grew 0.4%, with 2-wheeler growing strongly and private car and CV together down about 27%.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: CV share of motor fell to about 23-24% from roughly 65% four to five years ago, as the company deliberately exited the segment.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: GDPI down 37% against an industry decline of about 27-28%. Gross fire loss ratio was 67% in Q1 despite one large claim; retention is about 20%.

segments.name: Third-party motor
segments.commentary: TP loss ratio 66.6%, broadly stable. Market share was cut from April, with a view that a TP rate hike of 90-95% of vehicles is needed.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Loss ratio rose year on year, attributed to one large bank-driven personal accident policy. Group health and crop inward reinsurance were not renewed on pricing grounds.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not guide and will not assume that market conditions normalise in the current or next quarter.
Management is assuming soft market conditions persist at least until 31 March 2027.
Own damage loss ratio expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.
Management said that, excluding the drop in fire, the fourth quarter could see a base effect on growth.
Dividend: management said IGAAP solvency (about 242%) supports a dividend, to be considered by the Board in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms.
Underwriting and claims-settlement actions on TP were planned for around the third week of August 2026.
capex_capacity: Investment mix: 9.5% of AUM in equity, REITs and InvITs (AT1 bonds shown separately); management said it could take equity to 13-14% if markets fall, or to 15-18% in its stated framework.
Fixed income duration moved from 4.5 to 4.9 in Q1; reinvestment yield rose to 7.8% from 7.5%. Management said it would extend duration to about 5.2 if the 30-year yield moves above about 7.75%.
Reinsurance commission increased across all lines and reinsurance capacity increased, per management.
Management said it is waiting for RBC norms, expected possibly within FY27, to know whether solvency will be measured on RBC, IFRS or IGAAP.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing across most lines has fallen and is now down across the board. It cited EOM rules, which pushed commissions up, and low-priced crop, group health, and fire business written to meet EOM.
Claims inflation: no third-party motor rate increase for about five years, while minimum wages, parts, paint and labour costs have risen.
Fire rates were said to be down about 40-45%.
Management said Digit has not chased growth; it gave up fire and commercial business it judged underpriced, and said the 2W and bancassurance/digital channels were growing well.

Supreme Court (June 11, 2026) TP ruling: management said it is comfortable with reserves and will not take a bet on judgment interpretation; two High Court rulings (July 2 Allahabad, July 16 Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GDPI slowdown since listing size-driven or structural from industry and competitive change, and does it require investment in other channels or lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman attributed it to EOM rules pushing commissions up and low-priced crop, group health and fire business written to meet EOM; said Q1 is the first quarter Digit lost market share, and that bancassurance, institutional and digital/B2C channels are growing well. Management is assuming soft conditions persist until at least 31 March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the 11 June 2026 Supreme Court TP ruling on TP loss ratio and reserving, and is the step-up recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reserving is based on loss ratio plus legal inflation and frequency, with no separate provision; it is comfortable with reserves and takes no bet on judgment interpretation. Two High Court rulings (2 July Allahabad, 16 July Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling; underwriting and claim-settlement actions were planned for around the third week of August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Are there one-off or large losses in fire, marine and engineering this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman confirmed one large fire claim in Q1, but said gross fire loss ratio was 67%; he argued loss ratios are assessed on a gross basis because 80% of fire risk is ceded to reinsurers, and the company gives up treaty commission on some business to protect treaty profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IRDAI-driven TP hike needed, and what would be the quantum? What is the dividend policy given solvency and IFRS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 90-95% of vehicles need a TP premium hike, with a view that only about 5% of segments could see reductions; it is running the book without assuming a hike. On dividends, IGAAP solvency is about 242% and the Board will consider a dividend in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms (expected possibly this financial year).

qa_highlights.question: Is the TP claim-settlement approach (83% by compromise) adequate given 17% court awards, and will reserve releases be lower after the Supreme Court ruling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 36,000 TP claims settled since inception, 83% by compromise and 17% by court award; it reported reserve release of INR204 crore for FY18-19 falling to INR132 crore over later years, said no MAD concept is used, and declined to guide on future releases. Motor actuarial review of frequency was expected in 3-5 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the OD loss ratio increase, and why was it not anticipated?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said he took the wrong call by holding stand-alone OD renewals and new-car business written in FY24-25; the problem is in private car, not 2W or CV, and the portfolio was cut sharp from March. OD loss ratio is expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did group health loss ratio rise, and what drove NEP retention and EOM trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health rise was attributed to one large bank-driven personal accident policy, with claims provided for. Retention rose from a mix of higher retention in commercial lines and lower fire mix; EOM rose slightly at motor level due to exits from low-EOM fire and commercial business and non-renewal of group health and crop inward reinsurance.

risks_watch: Motor own damage loss ratio (73.3% group, private car driven) must stabilise in Q2 FY27 as guided; a miss would extend the margin pressure.
TP reserve adequacy post Supreme Court ruling (11 June 2026): watch the August 2026 underwriting and claim-settlement actions, the review petition, and further High Court interpretations.
Growth trajectory: GDPI down 8% (about -2% ex inward reinsurance); management expects a base effect from Q4 but gave no guidance and assumes soft market through 31 March 2027.
Investment-income dependence: equity raised to 9.5% of AUM at book value; unrealised equity gains of INR268 crore could reverse, and PBT was reduced by INR14 crore from the allocation shift.

Regulatory items: RBC norms timing and whether solvency is measured on RBC, IFRS or IGAAP; EOM, commission and distribution reforms; a possible TP premium hike that management says it has not assumed.
Fire: GDPI down 37% with rates down 40-45%; management says it has cut underpriced business, so watch fire retention and the treaty renewal.
key_quotes: We decided to focus on maintaining profitability. So for us, this is a soft quarter and much of it is soft by choice.
I would say in hindsight, I made the wrong call.
We do not chase growth. That does not pay for itself.
We don't take a bet. We basically look at where the market is.
544179|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and combative on strategy, with management openly framing Q1 as a deliberate choice of profitability over growth and admitting a wrong call on stand-alone OD renewals. It was cautious on guidance, declining to give any and avoiding quantification on TP reserve releases, while being evasive on the RBC and dividend timing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: GDPI fell 8% (about -2% ex inward reinsurance exits), motor market share fell to 5.6% from 6.25% in FY26, and management assumes soft market through 31 March 2027.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no formal guidance and assumes soft market conditions persist to 31 March 2027, with GDPI down 8% in Q1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Loss ratio rose 3pp to 73.3% and the OD fix is only guided for Q2 FY27, with TP reserve adequacy and August 2026 TP actions still open.

rows.label: TP premium hike of 90-95% of vehicles needed
rows.why: Management says 90-95% of vehicles need a TP premium hike and no TP rate increase has come in about five years, but the book is run without assuming one.

rows.why: IGAAP solvency is about 242% and the Board will consider a dividend in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms that may arrive within FY27.

rows.label: Motor OD loss ratio stabilisation

544181|2026-03.headline: Awfis FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR1,493 crore and EBITDA 37% to INR550 crore, with FY27 guided to 25-27% revenue growth.
544181|2026-03.overview: Awfis reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR1,493 crore (up 24% YoY) and operating EBITDA of INR550 crore (up 37%, margin 36.8%), with PAT before exceptionals up 66% to INR71 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR410 crore (up 21%) with EBITDA of INR152 crore (margin 37%). The company deliberately slowed seat additions to focus on Grade A/A+ premium centers, with gross seat additions of about 30,000 and net addition of about 22,000 in FY26. Design and build (Transform) revenue was softer, though its third-party business grew.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR11 crore in Q4 FY25 (+107%)

financial_highlights.value: INR655 crore before tax; INR616 crore net operating cash flow; normalized INR216 crore
Net cash through FY26; net debt to equity -0.20; gross debt to equity 0.09

segments.name: Coworking and allied services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,237 crore (+35% YoY); Q4 revenue INR342 crore (+27% YoY, +6% QoQ). Management said it met both revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY26.

segments.name: Awfis Transform (design and build)
segments.commentary: FY26 softer on project timing and fewer managed aggregation deals. Third-party revenue rose from INR95 crore (FY25) to INR152 crore (FY26), with third-party share at 59% (from 47%). Net D&B margin about 7-8%. INR130 crore of mandates won for delivery over the next 6-7 months.

segments.name: Frame by Awfis (furniture)
segments.commentary: Capex-light contract manufacturing across 5+ partners. Majority of new coworking centers to deploy Frame furniture by H1 FY27; 2-3 large external mandates targeted by H2 FY27.

segments.name: Others (facility management)
segments.commentary: Line item reflects the facility management business sold in September 2024; management does not expect further revenue from it.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 25-27%: coworking and allied 25-27% and Awfis Transform 22-25%.
FY27 gross seat additions guided at 22,000-25,000 seats (about 1.25 million sq ft), with capex broadly similar to FY26 levels for these seats.
Managed aggregation to stay around 60% of supply, with straight lease about 40%.
Mature-center occupancy (84%) targeted to rise by at least 100 bps over the next couple of quarters.
Margin expansion expected over 2-3 years from premiumization and a higher third-party share in D&B; no numeric margin target given.
Partial managed office and developer partnership pipelines expected to be meaningful supply pillars in FY27-FY28.
capex_capacity: Supply at FY26 end: 250 centers and about 167,000 seats in 18 cities; signed supply 266 centers and about 184,000 seats; operational capacity about 156,000-157,000 seats.
FY26 gross additions about 30,000 seats across 41 new centers, all in Grade A/A+; net addition about 22,000 seats after about 8,000 seats closed.
35 Gold and Elite centers at FY26 end (27 Gold, 8 Elite); premium footprint covers 8 GCC hubs including all 7 Tier 1 cities.
Partial managed office centers targeted at 30,000-50,000 sq ft; some deals up to 65,000-70,000 sq ft with 40-50% day-1 client demand.
Advanced talks with 2 institutional developers on partnerships with shared capex; over 4 lakh sq ft pre-committed under the MA model through Q2 FY28.
Awfis 6.0 design refresh expected to carry capex similar to 5.0 per seat; 6.0 to be the majority of seats added.
demand_pricing: Enterprise and MNC clients 64% of client base; average client tenure 37 months; lock-in tenure 26 months.
500-plus seat cohort 37% of portfolio; 48% of clients operate across multiple centers; clients in 10+ centers up 600 bps QoQ.
Blended occupancy 76% (up 300 bps over last four quarters on average seat base above 145,000); mature centers (over 12 months) 84%.
100-plus GCC clients across 9 cities contributing about 23% of rental revenue; 14 major GCC mandates closed in FY26, 6 already committed for FY27.
Revenue-to-rent ratio about 2.3x; revenue to gross fixed assets 1.5x.
Sold over 58,000 seats in FY26. Rent escalations: fixed for first 3 years, then 15% escalation per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross seat additions appear to be 26,000 when the sum of quarterly guidance was lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross additions were about 30,000 seats, with about 8,000 closed, giving a net addition of about 22,000 (157,000 operational seats vs about 135,000 a year earlier). Seat additions were kept low by a focus on quality over quantity.

qa_highlights.question: Will premiumization be a one-time shift, and what growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premiumization is now the default and non-negotiable, not a one-time step. Growth is driven by realization per seat, with FY27 revenue guided at about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of D&B and the revenue-to-rent ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: D&B net margins are about 7-8%. Revenue-to-rent ratio is about 2.3x.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in lease principal payments in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the 30,000 seats added in FY26 and late-FY25 centers coming off rent-free periods, plus renewal escalations. No average escalation percentage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the approximately 5% seat closure rate in FY26 a normal churn level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was a portfolio rebalancing year. About 3,000 seats were a single-client short-term setup, and the rest were exits at renewal or from older buildings below the Grade A+ bar. Management said 5% is not the churn rate it expects going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the gap between normalized rent and cash-flow rent widened?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the reconciling items from H1 persist, mainly operating lease items, which grow with time. He offered a one-on-one walkthrough and gave no quantified explanation on the call.

risks_watch: Lease principal outflows are rising with seat additions, rent-free expiries and renewal escalations; the cash-rent reconciliation gap widened to about INR60 crore in FY26 from about INR20 crore in H1.
Blended occupancy of 76% is dragged by ramping new centers; the 100 bps mature-cohort target is still to be delivered.
Seat additions of 22,000-25,000 in FY27 are well below the earlier 40,000 seat guidance, which was reduced in the quarter.
Design and build growth has been soft, and FY27 guidance of 22-25% depends on the INR130 crore order book converting.
Developer partnerships with 2 institutional developers are in advanced discussions but not signed.
Frame by Awfis is at an early stage, with external mandate targets for H2 FY27.
544181|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the strategy and FY26 delivery, with consistent emphasis on premiumization and ROCE. Less forthcoming on seat-addition reconciliation and the cash-rent gap, which management deferred to one-on-one follow-ups. Corrected its own FY27 guidance ranges for coworking and D&B during the call.
key_quotes: FY26 has been a defining year for Awfis. It was a year marked by strong execution, deeper enterprise adoption, sharper premiumization of the network and disciplined capital deployment.
Premiumization has now become default at Awfis, not a strategy overlay.
So the seat addition still is 30,000. It's because of some of the closures that have happened.
Yes. 5% is not the kind of a churn which we would look at.

rows.when: over next 2-3 years; H2 FY27 onward
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA margin 36.8% (up ~350 bps) on premiumization and higher third-party share in D&B (59% from 47%); management expects expansion over 2-3 years but gave no numeric target, and D&B net margin is only ~7-8%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gross seat additions guided at 22,000-25,000 (~1.25m sq ft) in FY27 vs ~30,000 gross in FY26; supply already signed at 266 centers/184,000 seats vs ~157,000 operational, so ~27,000 seats are in the pipeline.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Operational seats grew from ~135,000 to ~157,000 (+16%) and blended occupancy is 76%, with FY27 coworking revenue guided at 25-27%, though much of that is realisation per seat rather than seats.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex for FY27 seats guided broadly similar to FY26 (~INR208 crore); utilisation is only 76% so there is no capacity squeeze forcing a new capex announcement, but developer partnerships with shared capex (2 institutions, 4 lakh+ sq ft pre-committed) could bring a capex decision.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management corrected its FY27 ranges mid-call (coworking 25-27%, Transform 22-25%) and cut seat-addition guidance from ~40,000 to 22,000-25,000, so the bias is to hold rather than raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Transform FY27 growth of 22-25% depends on the INR130 crore order book converting over 6-7 months, and the 100 bps mature-centre occupancy uplift is not yet delivered; mature occupancy is 84% and blended 76%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Awfis 6.0 design refresh to be majority of seats added in FY27 and Frame furniture to be deployed in majority of new centers by H1 FY27; partial managed office formats (30,000-50,000 sq ft) planned in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Cash-rent gap and lease outflows widening
rows.why: Cash-rent reconciliation gap widened to about INR60 crore in FY26 from about INR20 crore in H1, and management deferred the explanation to one-on-one calls, so cash conversion quality is a watch item despite 1.01x operating cash flow to EBITDA.

rows.label: D&B order book conversion of INR130 crore
rows.why: INR130 crore of mandates won for delivery over 6-7 months against FY26 D&B revenue that was softer and FY27 Transform growth guided at 22-25%.

rows.label: Institutional developer partnerships
rows.why: Advanced talks with 2 institutional developers on shared-capex partnerships, with over 4 lakh sq ft pre-committed under MA model through Q2 FY28, but nothing signed yet.

tone.note: Management was confident on premiumization, FY26 delivery and FY27 growth of 25-27%, but cautious and deferred on the seat-addition reconciliation and the widening cash-rent gap; analysts pushed on seat additions, churn and cash-rent reconciliation.

544181|2026-06.headline: Awfis Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR425 crores and cash EBITDA reached INR44 crores, while blended occupancy held flat at 76%.
544181|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR425 crores and reported EBITDA rose 28% to INR162 crores (38.2% margin), with PBT of INR24 crores. Management introduced cash EBITDA as a new metric: INR44 crores (10.1% margin), up about 34% YoY. Occupancy was flat at 76% QoQ, though the mature cohort dipped to 83% from 84% after one enterprise client with about 3,000 seats across five centres exited. Management guided to FY27 cash EBITDA of INR190-200 crores, with H2 expected to outperform H1.

segments.name: Co-working and allied services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR352 crores, up 27% YoY. GCCs contribute 24% of rental revenue from 100+ unique GCC clients across nine cities.

segments.name: Transform (construction and fit-out)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR73 crores, up 25% YoY. Third-party share about 92% this quarter; management says blended margin is around 17-18% (15% on landlord-partner work, 18-20% on third-party). Over 200 crores of mandates won for FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross seat additions of 22,000-25,000.
Co-working revenue growth of 23-25% YoY for FY27.
Transform growth of about 20%; total FY27 revenue to exceed INR1,800 crores.
FY27 cash EBITDA of INR190-200 crores, with H2 better than H1 and Q4 expected to show a meaningful improvement in occupancy and margins.
FY27 capex of roughly INR200-210 crores.
Premium mix expected to move from about 85:15 to about 80:20 by end FY27, as about 10 of 13 pipeline properties are premium (Gold/Elite).
capex_capacity: Operational seats about 159,000 across 242 centres in 18 cities; 9 centres under fit-out (total 251); pipeline of 267 centres including LOIs.
Total capacity including fit-out about 170,000 seats; including signed LOIs over 185,000 seats.
Q1 gross seat additions about 4,600 against about 1,800 seats exited in portfolio consolidation.

Malpani Estates developer partnership (Pune, two Grade A+ assets, 1.4 lakh sq ft). Developer partnership centres expected to go live in 9-15 months; company contributes about 50% of fit-out value upfront as a security deposit; 9-year agreements.
Seven premium properties in the portfolio (two live, five under construction), priced 30-50% above the existing portfolio. Elite centres rose from 8 to 10; Gold held at 27.
Management expects over 12,000 seats on track in H1 FY27 across the three multiformat pillars.
demand_pricing: Active clients over 3,600; corporates and MNCs about 64% of base. Weighted average client tenure 38 months; average lock-in 26 months.
Mix by sector: technology 39%, professional services 21%, BFSI 13%, manufacturing 12%, healthcare and life sciences 5%. Domicile: 52% India-headquartered, 43% North American or European.
Clients with 500+ seats make up 37% of portfolio. Q1 sold 13,000 seats.
Blended occupancy 76% (flat QoQ); mature cohort (over 12 months old) 83%, down from 84%.
Pricing: 4-7% contractual escalation within same client; management says price per seat has risen every quarter over eight quarters. No exact figure given.
Replacement of vacated capacity: significant part pre-committed, some at higher pricing than the exited client paid.
Industry: H1 2026 flex leasing 8.4 million sq ft (+55%); GCC leasing 16.5 million sq ft (+38%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did rental payments jump from about INR85 crores in Q4 to about INR130 crores in Q1, and is the company shifting toward straight lease?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the cash-flow rent figure excludes rent booked in other expenses (MA profit shares and out-of-lock-in leases not under Ind AS 116); that line was flat, so combined growth is in line with indices. Management said MA is 57% of current supply (down from 62%), and the mix is opportunistic, not a shift away from MA.

qa_highlights.question: How do developer partnerships work: construction stage at signing, delivery timing, capital contribution and access period?
qa_highlights.answer: Centres could go live 9-15 months after signing. Company contributes about 50% of fit-out value on day one as a security deposit until go-live. Nine-year agreements start at signing, with the nine years counted from OC and possession.

qa_highlights.question: What is per-seat revenue trend given chargeable area growth versus revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 68% vs 65% comparison, because chargeable area includes unlive fit-out seats. Net operational seats rose 59% from about 100,000 to 159,000 against 65% revenue growth. Price per seat rises through 4-7% escalations and premium mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Transform's third-party share about 92%, and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Transform has shifted to third-party work; the 92% reflects this quarter's delivery mix and is expected to stay structurally high. Margins: about 15% on landlord-partner work and 18-20% on third-party, blending to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the implied FY27 cash EBITDA margin only about 10% when occupancy is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the exit of one large client, where the company kept fixed costs on five centres to refill them, and a timing gap of 3-4 quarters between landlord rent resets (many 2021 leases) and customer repricing. H2 is expected to be better, with Q4 showing a meaningful improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio is premium, and is the new supply institutional?
qa_highlights.answer: About 37 of 242 live centres (about 15%) are Gold/premium. Of the 13 properties in LOI or fit-out, about 10 are premium. The premium mix is expected to reach about 80:20 by end FY27. All pipeline assets are institutional.

risks_watch: Occupancy: blended 76% flat QoQ and mature cohort 83% (from 84%); management expects recovery via pre-committed replacement of the ~3,000 seats exited, but no timeline given beyond Q4 improvement.

Margin delivery: FY27 cash EBITDA guidance of INR190-200 crores implies roughly 10% margin; H1 is weak (3-4 quarter lag between landlord rent resets and customer repricing), so H2/Q4 step-up must materialise.

Lease mix shift: MA share fell to 57% from 62%, with more developer partnerships and selective lease (rent cash outflow up to ~INR130 crores from ~INR85 crores QoQ per analyst); watch rent cost and fixed-cost exposure.
Transform: third-party share at ~92% and blended margin 17-18% (15% landlord-partner vs 18-20% third-party); watch mix sustainability and margin trend.

qa_highlights.question: Is there early visibility on Q3 flight trends?

qa_highlights.question: What GTV mix can be expected over 3-4 years, and will rail share gains continue?

qa_highlights.question: How much of a threat do consumer AI agents pose, and which segments are most exposed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-platform traffic is still a low single-digit share and sees specialist vertical agents, and ixigo's proprietary data and peace-of-mind products as differentiators. Building products is easy; trust and distribution are the hard parts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus growth of about 28% too slow given supply and rail constraints?

544198|2026-03.headline: DEE Development FY26 revenue rose 38% to Rs 1,142 Cr and PAT 76.9% to Rs 77.2 Cr; order book Rs 2,040 Cr with FY27 inflow guided above Rs 2,000 Cr.

Management split the business into core (piping, heavy fabrication) and non-core (power, biomass pallets), with core EBITDA of Rs 210.5 Cr (+64.2%) excluding non-core losses. 544198|2026-06.headline: DEE Development Engineers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to Rs 294.5 crore and EBITDA margin hit 16.9%, despite ~Rs 25 crore of dispatches slipping into Q2.

Management said about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches, deferred by export customers amid Middle East disruption, moved into Q2. Profit after tax was Rs 16.1 crore, and the Rs 300 crore preferential issue (net ~Rs 293 crore, ~Rs 225 crore earmarked for debt repayment) closed in July. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ revenue, EBITDA margin above 19%, and order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore.

544202|2026-03.headline: Stanley Lifestyles FY26 gross margin rose 151 bps to 57.5%, but Q4 revenue fell on B2B export pull-down and management guides only conservative FY27 growth.

Q4 FY26 saw a decline in B2B demand from mid-Q4, with roughly Rs. 15 crore of B2B revenue pulled down due to West Asia conflict disruptions to a large export client. Gross margin for FY26 improved to 57.5% from 56.3%, while cash was about Rs. 200 crore versus Rs. 215 crore a year earlier despite capex above Rs. 60 crore. Management opened 11 stores and closed three over 12 months, and guided to aspirational double-digit growth but a conservative stance for FY27.

544210|2026-03.headline: Emcure FY26 revenue crossed INR9,204 crore (+16.6%), but Q4 domestic growth slowed to 5.2% on Zuventus disruption; FY27 guided to low-to-mid-teen growth.
544210|2026-03.overview: Emcure reported FY26 revenue of INR9,204 crore (+16.6% YoY), with adjusted PAT up 41% to INR1,008 crore and EBITDA margin up 80 bps to 19.4%. Q4 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,470 crore, but domestic growth slowed to 5.2% because of attrition and restructuring at the newly consolidated Zuventus business. International markets grew 25.7% in Q4, with Europe and Canada leading. Management said April is on plan and guided FY27 to low-to-mid-teen revenue growth and 75-100 bps of EBITDA margin expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +24.5% YoY; margin up from 18.4% in Q4 FY25
Up YoY due to Manx payouts and Zuventus minority stake buyout

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR4,027 crore (+10%), led by women's health, cardio, CNS and oncology. Q4 revenue INR977 crore (+5.2%) was hit by Zuventus. Management said ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% and the full-year ex-Zuventus base growth was high single digit.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR5,177 crore (+22.2%). Q4 revenue INR1,493 crore (+25.7%); currency added roughly 7-8% overall, about 11-12% in Europe.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,850 crore (+25.5%). Q4 revenue INR538 crore (+35.8%), helped by Manx and Amphotericin B. Management expects mid-teens CAGR over the next two years.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,487 crore (+18.7%). Q4 revenue INR399 crore (+28.6%), driven by market share gains and launches.

segments.commentary: FY26 ROW revenue INR1,840 crore (+21.8%), with ARV and non-ARV both contributing. Q4 emerging markets revenue INR556 crore (+15.5%).

qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year ex-Zuventus base growth would have been 9-10%, and Q4 ex-Zuventus was below 8%. It expects the impact to fade, with April back on track.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.

segments.name: India

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 537 crore, +32.8% YoY, driven by base business and liposomal amphotericin B (Ampho). Ampho is introduced in pretty much all countries, but tender-based procurement means lumpy orders.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 427 crore, +24.6% YoY, on new launches and share gains. Semaglutide filing expected in the next few months; Quebec launch via Dr. Reddy's is uncertain.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 522 crore, +44.8% YoY, led by ARV. About two-thirds of ROW was ARV this quarter; management expects ARV at about 50-55% of ROW for the full year.

qa_highlights.answer: Filing expected in the next few months, delayed because semaglutide was pursued as a global development. Quebec timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply; management will defer to them.

qa_highlights.answer: Mix from Europe and ARV growth; FY27 gross margin guided at about 59%. Management says B2B international businesses are EBITDA-accretive despite lower gross margin.
