Weighted average cost of debt (operational projects)
financial_highlights.change: Refinancing cut rate by ~150 bps on INR3,300 crore

segments.name: Solar and wind generation (operational)
segments.commentary: Operational contracted generation capacity is 2,990 MW. Management said plant and grid availability were above 99% for the year, and FY26 portfolio CUF was about 26%. Sikar (Rajasthan) new plants ran at about 29-30% CUF for the year, and roughly 28%+ in Q4.

segments.name: BESS (merchant)
segments.commentary: About 2.3 GWh of BESS is commissioned, mostly in March, and earns about INR2.2 crore per day net (over INR60 crore per month) from tariff arbitrage. Round-trip efficiency is 88-90%. Management said the Q3 battery contribution was negligible.

guidance_outlook: Target of about 1.5 GW of generation projects commissioned in FY27, with the first FDRE commissioning at Neemuch substation in June 2026.

Battery target of about 10 GWh for the next calendar year: roughly 8.5 GWh merchant and 1.5 GWh in FDRE format. Management said the 10 GWh target is achievable on connectivity and financing; supply and geopolitics are the main uncertainties.
Around 2.5 GW of connectivity at operational substations (Fatehgarh-1, Fatehgarh-2 under STOA, Bikaner-3) is ready for BESS discharge at night.
Under-construction portfolio of 5.1 GW (total pipeline 8,071 MW) with PPA-signed capacity of 3,280 MW; PPA-signed projects expected to be commissioned by FY28.
Management expects a run-rate EBITDA jump as battery revenue starts; a 75-80% EBITDA margin is expected on merchant BESS at INR6 tariff arbitrage.
capex_capacity: Committed total capex INR12,475 crore: INR6,445 crore incurred in FY26 and INR6,030 crore in purchase orders. Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in Q4.
Gross block rose about INR3,460 crore in FY26, of which about INR1,000-1,100 crore is battery.

Capital advances of about INR323 crore, mainly battery (10% advance against bank guarantee) and turbines (20% advance). Management said solar module capex is being deferred until the LTA is operational.
Under-construction portfolio added 301 MW of peak-power FDRE with SECI in the quarter; total under construction is 5.1 GW, requiring about 17 GWh of BESS.

Commissioning timeline: NTPC hybrid solar ready, LTA by December 2026; Pachora wind component a couple of quarters later; SJVN Fatehgarh full FDRE by FY27 end (LTA March 2027). Pavagada and Anantapur are targeted this year per CTU timelines.
demand_pricing: India peak demand hit 256 GW on 25 April 2026, against 250 GW in May 2024. Electricity consumption grew 8.9% in April 2026.

India added about 55 GW of RE in FY26 (cumulative 283 GW). Management expects peak-power and FDRE/BESS-linked bids to dominate, with 15-20 GW of bids this year (fewer than last year) and state plus central tenders of 20-30 GW.

Management said peak-power products sell fastest, followed by partial peak, then wind; plain solar sells slowest. Thermal-equivalent BESS pricing is cited at INR9-10 per unit at peak, with the annual realisation at INR7-8.
Receivable days have fallen to about 14-15 days from about 180 days in the past. Trade receivables fell 13% YoY. Central offtakers take a cash discount and pay in about 10 days.

qa_highlights.question: What battery capex was incurred and how much BESS capacity was commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in the last quarter, and about 1.3 GWh was commissioned as of the prior quarter. Battery capacity reached 2.3 GWh by the time of the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the run-rate EBITDA from existing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 EBITDA including other income was about INR2,200 crore, mainly from the PPA projects. BESS revenue at INR2.2 crore per day is over INR60 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is there curtailment, and how is future project allocation shaped?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 2 projects are connected to the state grid. FY26 curtailment impact was INR5-6 crore, plus INR3 crore of STU impact in Rajasthan. Nearly all of the portfolio is on CTU, with the goal that each project has a battery.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross block growing faster than run-rate EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,000-1,100 crore of the gross block increase is battery, and the battery was commissioned late in the year, so it is not yet in run-rate EBITDA. Wind is also still ramping in phases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from LOA conversion and CERC connectivity rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 6.2 GW of signed PPAs are under construction, and 3.2 GW of LOA has converted to PPA. Management does not expect LOAs to be surrendered, and it has a backup plan of using connectivity for future bids or battery-linked projects.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the BESS arbitrage last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duration is uncertain. It estimated the national need at about 200-300 GWh, and said the peak price should stay at INR7-8 for four to five years given gas constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Are CTU substation delays affecting commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 60% of substations are on time and the maximum delay is typically 6 months. Where delays are known, modules are deferred, and no penalty applies under the sync-up framework.

risks_watch: Commissioning timelines depend on CTU substations and LTA dates; management cites delays of up to about 6 months, with the 1.5 GW FY27 target at risk.
BESS merchant revenue depends on the peak-offpeak price spread; management concedes the duration is uncertain and the spread could narrow as more batteries come online.
The 10 GWh battery target depends on supply of material and geopolitical factors.
CERC draft proposal on LOA-based connectivity and PPA signing risk for about 850 MW of older PPAs still in discussion.
Q4 PLF fell about 1% YoY, which management attributed to lower irradiation and curtailment.
Management commentary on the new CFO is that Arun Chopra has replaced Rajat Kumar Singh; watch for continuity.

So technically, maybe 25 to 30 gigawatt will technically mean solar of 40, 50 gigawatt.
So 6 month s delay is, I think, very much -- should be taken in a good light.

544283|2026-06.headline: ACME Solar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to INR954 crore and EBITDA 56% to INR831 crore, with BESS contributing INR226 crore.
544283|2026-06.overview: Management reported record revenue and EBITDA for Q1 FY27, with total revenue of INR954 crore (up 63% YoY), EBITDA of INR831 crore (up 56%) and PAT of INR235 crore (up 80%). Growth was attributed to a record CUF of 30.9%, BESS revenue and new renewable capacity. BESS commissioning reached about 3.62 GWh cumulative, and the BESS commissioning guidance was pulled forward to more than 10 GWh by FY27 from calendar 2027. Management also said it has locked in about INR1,400 crore of short-term BESS revenue for FY27 and addressed a fire at the ACME Suryodaya BESS site, attributing it to an AC cabling short circuit rather than the battery system.

financial_highlights.change: Lower due to charging power cost in opex

segments.name: Renewable energy (solar/FDRE)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin ~88-89% in Q1; ex-BESS EBITDA margin stated at ~91%, with seasonal range of 88-91% over recent quarters. Management cited repowering of existing plants as a margin support.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR226 crore in Q1 with ~82% EBITDA margin; cumulative commissioned capacity ~3.62 GWh (about 40% of India's cumulative commissioned BESS). Management cites an annual EBITDA-to-capex yield above 20%.

guidance_outlook: BESS commissioning target raised to more than 10 GWh by FY27 (earlier: 10 GWh by calendar 2027), roughly three quarters earlier.
Around 1.5 GW of contracted renewable capacity to be commissioned in FY27, subject to substation and transmission availability.
Full-year FY27 capex upgraded to approximately INR15,000-20,000 crore.
About INR1,400 crore of BESS revenue locked for FY27 on roughly 70-80% of the ~10 GWh target; management said it could be higher if more volume is contracted.
Management indicated a 2-3 year assumption of INR1,400 crore-plus BESS revenue is reasonable; BESS EBITDA margin expected within 2-5% of Q1 level (~82%).
Management said it may increase its 2030 target beyond 10 GWh, to be updated in coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio 8,070 MW, with about 20 GWh of battery storage; under-construction capacity 5,080 MW.
PPAs signed for 3,880 MW, including 600 MW of new FDRE and hybrid PPAs with SECI this quarter; about 1,200 MW still awaiting PPA signing.
Debt tied up for about 85% of PPA-signed portfolio; INR6,000 crore financing secured for 700 MW of under-construction FDRE projects.
Battery procurement: more than 15 GWh ordered (CATL, Hithium); around 90% of the 20 GWh battery requirement contracted, with orders placed where PPAs are signed.

BESS capex ~INR93 lakh per MW including transformer, IDC and EPC; management said it could rise 5-10% for future batches. More than $300 million hedged at roughly $89-93 per unit of USD exchange rate.
Battery operations: round-trip efficiency ~89%, depth of discharge ~93%, state of health above 99.9%, availability above 99%; operating at one cycle per day.
demand_pricing: India power demand grew 8.8% YoY in Q1 to 485 billion units; peak demand hit a record 271 GW and was near 270 GW in July.
Short-term BESS realisations cited at INR8-10/kWh (publicly available DEEP portal and HP-TAM bids), sometimes higher; contracts are typically under one year, with 6-9 months' lead time.
Open (merchant) BESS capacity is about 600 MWh; management aims for zero open capacity outside PPA by end-2026, though a 300 MW plant is still open.

SECI is consolidating bids and will only bid with firmer power-offtake commitments, reducing near-term bid volumes; management expects large FDRE, peak power, CFD and state bids to follow over 6-9 months.
Management sees the peak-power market growing toward 300-500 GWh, potentially 1 TWh in a positive case, driven by rooftop and KUSUM solar (duck-curve effect).
Competition from other BESS entrants (including Adani) is rising, but management argues merchant supply will remain limited and that the market is still new to state buyers.

qa_highlights.question: How much open or early BESS capacity will there be in FY27 and the next couple of years, and what are realisations on the INR1,400 crore short-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is contracting well above 10 GWh and realisations are INR8-10 per unit, depending on month and volume. Only ~600 MWh is open today, with a target of zero open capacity outside PPAs by end-2026. Management plans for 10-12 GWh to remain available for short-term markets each year over the next five years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the curtailment impact and what drove EBITDA growth ex-BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment was about 1% of revenue, only on state-based projects. EBITDA growth was attributed to CUF (30.9% vs 28.5%) and repowering of existing plants. Management is considering adding batteries to state projects to absorb surplus generation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,400 crore revenue sustainable for 2-3 years, given El Nino-driven pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the 10 GWh base supporting INR1,400 crore-plus for the next 2-3 years based on PPA and GNA timelines. Beyond that, it depends on market pricing and new PPAs. It said the market is still untapped by most discoms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core (ex-BESS) EBITDA margin and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-BESS margin was ~91% in Q1, with a seasonal range of 88-91%. Management expects FDRE projects may lift margins because their realisations are healthier than plain solar.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 6.28 INR/kWh PPA and the hybrid configuration changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The hybrid project was offered with 1 hour of battery, a change from the standard configuration. The other project at INR6.28 per unit has no change in configuration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for C&I and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has started hiring for data-centre opportunities but is focused on profitability. It intends to target CTU-connected C&I customers and will not dilute mid-to-high teen return targets.

544285|2026-06.headline: Swiggy guides Quick Commerce contribution margin to 0 to -100 bps for growth, with 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior.
544285|2026-06.overview: Swiggy's Q1 FY27 call (held July 30, 2026) centred on a deliberate pivot from contribution-margin protection to growth in Quick Commerce (Instamart). Management said it reached contribution margin breakeven, closing the last quarter at -0.2%, and now guides to a 0 to -100 bps range to fund store expansion, speed, serviceability and assortment. Take-rate gains were attributed to brand monetisation, advertising and user-fee changes, with management calling them sustainable. Food delivery growth was about 18% adjusted for cancellations, with 18-20% YoY guidance maintained, and management dismissed zero-commission competition from Toing's rivals as unsustainable. Toing, the new value-led food platform, is loss-making and was a major focus, with a Capital Markets Day planned for the following week.

segments.commentary: Adjusted growth about 18% YoY; YoY guidance 18-20% maintained. Take rate about 3%, with a target of 5%; management expects steady margin accretion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the food delivery zero-commission model a threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Kapoor argued zero commission is not sustainable; costs must be recovered from restaurants, consumers or delivery partners. Competition is expected in affordability, not premium.

qa_highlights.answer: Annual salary revision sits below CM. Minimum wage hikes in some states affect picking and packing; impact described as not material. Last-mile cost rose on seasonal factors including elections and harvest migration; efficiency offset kept the YoY dip to 20 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Are competitors capitalising costs or securitising payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Bothra said Swiggy does not capitalise employee, tech token or store costs, and is not aware of payables securitisation practices by peers.

qa_highlights.answer: Growth from transacting users and frequency; more stores in existing cities as hyper-local stores hit 2,500-3,000 orders/day. Spend priorities are store expansion, speed and serviceability, and selection availability.

544285|2026-09.headline: Swiggy Q2 FY27: Quick commerce NOV grew 13.4% QoQ with 1.3 million MTUs added, while Toing investment stays range-bound and food margin target of 5% of GOV is reaffirmed.

Toing, the affordability platform, is being run as a range-bound investment; management asked for another quarter or two before judging whether it is a scalable model. 544286|2026-03.headline: Niva Bupa FY26 GWP grew 27.4% to INR9,433 crores and IFRS PAT rose to INR366 crores; FY29 combined ratio target ~99%.
544286|2026-03.overview: FY26 closed with 27.4% overall GWP growth to INR9,433 crores (retail +35%) and Ind AS PAT of INR366 crores versus INR203 crores, with ROE at 10.7%. Expense of management fell to 33.7% from 39.2%, and the IFRS combined ratio improved 160 bps to 101.4% despite a 1.1 pt rise in loss ratio. Retail market share rose to 10.1% for the full year and 10.4% in Q4. Management set a long-term IFRS combined ratio target of about 99% by FY29, which it says translates to a mid-to-high teens ROE. Commission regulation remains an open question pending regulator guidance.

financial_highlights.change: improved 160 bps; loss ratio up 1.1 pts, expense ratio down 2.7 pts
from 39.2% last year; allowable EOM ~36% incl. additional allowances
growth slowed in FY26 vs prior two years, attributed to capital raise timing
1H FY26 68.1%, 9M 66.9%; YoY deterioration ~80 bps per analyst

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: FY26 retail growth 35%; H2 retail growth above 40% vs industry ~30%. Retail mix of new to renewal roughly 40:60; portfolio share 20-25%. Renewal book combined ratio ~97-98%.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Group loss ratio ~60.5% for FY26. Group split roughly one-third corporate and two-thirds Banca-based, unchanged. Analyst noted onerous-contract loss components were recognised at 9M and were unwound in Q4.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Retail bank business growing ~46% in new business per management. Asset cross-sell model viewed as de-risked under RBI guidance. Long-term policies about 20% of retail business.

guidance_outlook: Long-term IFRS combined operating ratio target of ~99% by FY29, with loss ratio flat to up 100-150 bps and savings from expense ratio, translating to a mid-to-high teens ROE (~11% currently).

Expense ratio savings expected to come from business mix shift to renewals, fixed overhead growing ~6-7% against GWP growth, and technology/Gen AI investments; management cited 2-2.5% expense benefit.
Industry retail health CAGR of 17-19% over five years, unchanged view.
Plan to take common empanelment network from 2,500 hospitals toward 5,000 in the next 4-5 months, excluding top-20 hospital groups.
Full IFRS accounts and annexures to be published on website around next week.
capex_capacity: Distribution: net addition of 58,000 agents, 50+ brokers and 23 additional financial institutions added in FY26.
Bharat strategy via own virtual agency and bank distribution into Tier 3 and below; expansion to more geographies planned in FY27.
Preferred provider network in 49 cities with 1,000+ hospitals; ~20% of claims in these cities go through them.
30+ generative AI, analytics and technology pilots or projects underway across the value chain.
Ind AS 117 (IFRS 17) effective April 2026; company goes live from the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Ticket size grew ~14-14.5% in the last six months vs first six months, driven by GST-related premium effects on both fresh and renewal business; management said all retail channels saw ticket-size growth.
Volume growth of 24% alongside 35% retail value growth; agent GWP per policy is the relevant metric per management.
Commission ratio on Indian GAAP fell sequentially due to senior citizen commission cut from 1 April 2025 and GST impact.
Management argues lower prices expand volume and value (citing GST experience) and would keep distributors remunerated if commission caps come.
Industry-wide: GST removal on retail health cited as a tailwind; Achha Kiya Insurance Liya awareness campaign is multi-year.

qa_highlights.question: What building blocks are needed to scale GWP from ~INR9,000 crores to INR15,000-16,000 crores at 25% growth, and what steady-state IFRS expense ratio is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from existing multichannel distribution, product segments covering almost all income segments except poor, and Bharat/Tier 3 expansion. Long-term IFRS combined ratio target ~99% by FY29 with expense-driven savings.

qa_highlights.question: How would the company respond to potential commission caps or cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management awaits regulator guidance and prefers retaining a single expense of management limit with a possible glide path lower. It said distributors would be appropriately remunerated and volume growth would offset any impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indian GAAP expenses reverse at shareholder account?
qa_highlights.answer: Excess EOM was transferred from policyholder to shareholder account until 31 December; full-year EOM compliance led to reversal. Management called it an optical, contra-entry item with no net impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is retail claims ratio trend sustainable and what drives its improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonality from post-monsoon infections exists; plan assumes some basis-point worsening offset by operating leverage. Management said quality is improving and incidence, claim sizes are in line with plan. Renewal book combined ratio ~97-98%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are onerous contract loss components recognised, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Under IFRS, loss components are created when expected loss ratio, expenses and risk adjustment exceed 100%; a 9M loss component was unwound in Q4 and similar amounts existed in the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: How will the common empanelment and standard treatment protocols benefit the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Protocols are live for seven infections, with 144 standard treatment workflows; top-20 groups deliberately excluded in Phase 1 with the focus on mid-size hospitals to widen access. Benefits expected via care pathway and length-of-stay standardisation.

risks_watch: Commission regulation: any cap or cut on expense of management could affect distribution economics; regulator guidance awaited.
Retail loss ratio trend (66.8% FY26) and seasonal post-monsoon claims; management resists targeting a lower claims ratio.
Recognition of onerous contract loss components at group health under IFRS 17, which can swing quarterly results.
Slower AUM growth in FY26 tied to capital raise timing; management says underlying growth is steady.
Banca regulatory scrutiny (RBI); management says the bank channel is de-risked by cross-sell structure.
Industry growth normalising from the H2 GST-led surge; long-term industry retail CAGR view 17-19%.

Answers on claims ratio and onerous contracts were framed defensively, with management stressing optical or accounting explanations.
key_quotes: And in Q4 specifically, we moved our market share to 10.4%, up from 9%.
So, our belief and prayers to the authority continues to be around keeping a single limit of expense of management and maybe a glide path to lower that.
That 99% combined ratio will translate to mid- to high teens ROE, which is close to 11% currently.
But this is optical only, there is a contra entry so it doesn't change anything.

rows.why: Asset-light insurer; no utilisation or capex figures discussed in the brief.

rows.why: Network goes from 2,500 to 5,000 hospitals (excluding top-20 groups), which management links to care pathway and length-of-stay standardisation for claims.

rows.why: Ticket size grew ~14-14.5% in the last six months vs the first six, across all retail channels, though this tailwind may normalise as the H2 GST-led surge fades.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, market share and the FY29 ~99% combined ratio path, but non-committal on commission regulation and defensive on the retail claims ratio and onerous contract losses, with analysts probing those areas.

544286|2026-06.headline: Niva Bupa Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR137.8 crore and CISR improved 300bp to 100.2%, driven by a 3.8pp lower loss ratio.
544286|2026-06.overview: Niva Bupa reported Q1 FY27 profit after tax of INR137.8 crore and a combined insurance service ratio (CISR) of 100.2%, against 103.2% a year earlier. Growth was strong in retail health (reported 47.1%, like-to-like 35.5%) while group business was flat amid a challenging B2B pricing environment. The company moved fully to Ind AS in Q1, with parallel IFRS 17-style disclosures continuing for public reporting. Management said July loss ratio trends were in line with plan and reiterated the FY29 mid-to-high-teens ROE target.

financial_highlights.change: +90bp, mainly retail mix shift and GST ITC loss

financial_highlights.value: INR9,963 crore book value; over INR10,000 crore MTM

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: Retail reported growth 47.1% (like-to-like 35.5%); quarter growth 46.5% per management, with fresh up 41%. Retail mix of fresh to renewal about 35:65; renewal loss ratio around 75%, with high single-digit annual renewal price increases.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Group growth flat in Q1 as the company declined large group accounts outside its underwriting philosophy and faced B2B pricing pressure; SME growing 50%+. Management said industry group pricing is at claims-minus levels.

guidance_outlook: Targets retail growth 8-10 percentage points above market growth; management said July momentum was good but declined to forecast in detail.
CISR and ROE trajectory: ROE near 12% annualised now, targeted at mid-to-high teens by FY29; FY29 guidance reiterated.
EoM ratio expected to settle around 32-33% over time from 35.2% in Q1.
Expense ratio distortion from GST ITC loss and reinsurance profit-commission timing expected to normalise from Q3 FY27, with YoY comparability thereafter.
Internal retail:group mix target of roughly 70:30 unchanged.
Board approved debt raising committee and enabling resolution for up to INR500 crore; INR250 crore NCD call option due this fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Distribution: advisor network expansion continued at last year's pace, with new smaller-town locations (Bharat initiative); investment run-rate unchanged for six years, though incremental spend is smaller given company size.
Preferred Provider Network (PPN) present in 49 cities with more than 1,000 hospitals; 22% of claims flow through these hospitals.
Health partner app: about 570,000 monthly active users; over 62,000 monthly health check/diagnostic bookings and over 6,600 monthly doctor consults.
Investment book: AIF commitment about 4% of AUM vs 5% regulatory cap; Nifty ETFs about 3.5% of investment book; no direct equity plans at this stage.
GenAI initiatives in production, built in-house via AI Lab and through third-party products.
demand_pricing: Retail growth 46.5% in Q1 with both fresh (41%) and renewal growing; management aims to grow 8-10pp above market.

Group business: no growth in Q1; challenging B2B pricing with industry pricing at claims-minus per management; company not averse to group but will only write within its combined-ratio threshold, which it has not met for the last year or this quarter.
Industry: retail health grew 31.6%, total health 22.4% on reported basis; industry awareness spend about INR120 crore a year, roughly half on health.

PPN claims: management says secondary-care network claims are 15-20% lower in average claim size than tertiary/quaternary for the same treatment; differential quoted as 15-30pp depending on procedure. Management cautioned that PPN savings may be passed to customers via pricing rather than retained as better loss ratio.
Reassure 3.0 product launched August last year and cited as a growth driver.

qa_highlights.question: What is the July loss ratio trend and outlook for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: July is in line with expectations with no unusual trend; infection season risk is still ahead and will be updated next quarter. Y-o-Y loss ratio gains came from retail new business mix and from exiting large group accounts that did not fit underwriting norms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net reinsurance expense rise sharply, and will expense ratios normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Reinsurance line moves are timing of profit commission on quota-share treaties; no structural change expected and it should converge to historical trend through the year. GST-related ITC loss on expenses normalises from Q3, after which YoY comparisons should be clean.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a trend change that could sustain growth above the market?
qa_highlights.answer: No structural change; distribution and product levers continue, targeting 8-10pp above market growth in retail. Group growth held back by pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Does PPN reduce the loss ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: PPN lowers claim size by 15-20% vs tertiary care, but management said it may be used to price more competitively rather than to improve the loss ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What are fresh vs renewal splits in retail, and how is the renewal loss ratio trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail mix about 35% fresh and 65% renewal; renewal loss ratio about 75%, acceptable given expenses of under 20% on that book, with annual high-single-digit price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise INR500 crore of debt and any equity shift in investments?
qa_highlights.answer: INR250 crore NCD (raised 5 years ago at 10.7% coupon when rated A) has its call option due; the rest funds growth plans. ICRA issuer rating is AAA and an instrument rating is coming. No change in investment strategy; AIFs (mostly performing credit, 12-15% yield) being built toward the 5% cap.

risks_watch: Infection season ahead: management said it will update on infection behaviour next quarter, and flagged that abnormal infection would be the main deviation from the planned loss ratio trajectory.
Monsoon and flood-related claims: management said it must 'see through the monsoon'; July was described as range-bound versus plan, with some upside already built into the plan.
Group pricing: industry group pricing is at claims-minus levels, the company has not met its combined-ratio threshold for the last year or this quarter, and group growth was flat in Q1.

Expense ratio normalisation: GST ITC loss and reinsurance profit-commission timing are expected to normalise from Q3 FY27; the net reinsurance expense line rose sharply in Q1 and its timing effect will need to be tracked.
Second-half base effect: management said retail growth on an elevated GST-driven base was not forecast in detail; July momentum was described as good but not quantified.

Renewal book: renewal loss ratio of around 75% relies on high single-digit annual price increases; PPN claim-size savings may be passed to customers via pricing rather than retained in the loss ratio.
key_quotes: Our profit after tax improved to INR137.8 crores in Q1. Our combined insurance service ratio improved to 100.2%, which is a significant improvement over the 103.2% that we had for Q1 last year.
The market is operating at claims minus in terms of pricing, annualized claims forecasted minus. Obviously, that makes no economic sense.
Claims ratios is also a choice driven by the repricing and the extent of repricing that we need to do. This gives us flexibility, on that aspect.
So in retail, renewal loss ratio 75% is quite acceptable because expenses are not that much in that book.
What we guided earlier was by FY '29 mid to high teens, and we go by that.
544286|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operating trends and the FY29 ROE target, which was reiterated, but cautious on forecasting: management declined to quantify July growth and repeatedly deferred on infection and monsoon outcomes. Defensive on group business, where it said it will not write below its combined-ratio threshold despite pressure on growth.

rows.why: Board approved up to INR500 crore debt raising enabling resolution; INR250 crore NCD (10.7% coupon) has its call option due this fiscal year and ICRA issuer rating is AAA.

544288|2026-03.headline: BlackBuck FY26 total income rose about 55% to ~715 crore and adjusted EBITDA reached ~190 crore, with first full-year PAT of ~160 crore.
544288|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of about 715 crore (up ~55% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of about 190 crore (up ~84%) and PAT of about 160 crore, the first full year of profitability. Q4 FY26 total income grew ~46-52% YoY, adjusted EBITDA was 50.2 crore (up ~30% YoY) and net revenue grew ~31%. Management flagged short-term headwinds from the West Asia conflict on intercity trucking and a temporary suspension of OMC fuel loyalty programmes, while stating long-term retention, ARPU and acquisition are unchanged. Investment in growth businesses (super loads, vehicle finance) continued to weigh on margins, and management declined to give numerical growth guidance.

financial_highlights.change: first full year of PAT profitability
core businesses ~30% YoY in Q4, ~34% for FY
management says it tracks adjusted EBITDA

financial_highlights.metric: Power users (using more than two services)

financial_highlights.value: peaked ~36% in Q1 FY26, stabilised ~31% (per analyst)

segments.name: Core businesses (tolling, fuelling, fuel sensor, vehicle tracking, AIS/GPS)
segments.commentary: Core grew ~30% YoY in Q4 and ~34% for FY26. Tolling GTV grew ~27% YoY, about 90% of payments GTV. AIS device sales doubled QoQ on mandates; basic GPS growing ~15%.

segments.name: Growth businesses (super loads, vehicle finance)
segments.commentary: Growth businesses grew roughly 300% YoY in Q4 per management. Vehicle finance disbursals grew 30% in the prior quarter and a further 25% in Q4; super loads run-rate net revenue is ~15 crore vs ~10-11 crore a few quarters back (per analyst).

guidance_outlook: No numerical growth guidance; management said it has decided not to guide on numbers.
Short-term drag on growth expected from West Asia conflict, mainly on intercity heavy-truck movement; April-May saw drag after inventory moved through March.
Fuel business affected by temporary OMC loyalty programme suspension; some impact absorbed in Q4, some expected in Q1 FY27.
Management expects long-term retention, ARPU and customer acquisition to be unaffected.
Vehicle finance expected to exit investment mode and start generating cash flows by end FY27 (per management).
capex_capacity: Continued investment in growth businesses; teams and product/technology headcount being added in parallel experiments, with AI investment in super loads.
Super loads operating in Bangalore and Hyderabad hubs, plus 10 new cities launched earlier; team scaling continuing in existing cities.
Vehicle finance is asset-light: ~600 crore assets managed by partners, of which ~10% on BlackBuck's own books, used mainly for experiments and co-lending.
demand_pricing: Monthly transacting customers ~8.2 lakh, claimed 25-30% of Indian truckers; 10,000+ offline touchpoints; trucker spends ~45 minutes daily on the platform.
Intercity trucking demand softened in April-May 2026 due to West Asia conflict; revenue largely compounding so impact seen as small but visible.
Telematics: AIS demand driven by mandates in 10 states; basic GPS and cannibalisation by AIS noted.

Management said MLFF is prepaid-based, with 99%+ of payments prepaid per offline information; BlackBuck's revenue is 100% from issuer ecosystem today and it is exploring acquirer-side partnerships in MLFF.
Working capital: over 50% of telematics revenue received in advance; receivables under 3 months; other businesses under 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: Are super load hubs (Bangalore, Hyderabad) at break-even, and are existing cities still being staffed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit economics are strengthening as manpower tenures; teams are being scaled rapidly in existing cities as well, and it did not quantify break-even.

qa_highlights.question: Vehicle finance book size and whether BlackBuck has a right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: About 600 crore managed by partners with ~10% on BlackBuck's books; differentiation is digital distribution and data, with 24-48 hour onboarding, but management said the model is not expected to be non-linear as it is a risk business for partners.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit margins soften and what growth can be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed higher investment in growth businesses; said growth is an outcome of acquisition economics and it will not provide growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: When will super loads revenue scale from ~5 crore incremental to tens of crores, and cost base rise from ~70-75 to ~100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted pace could have been faster; said a significant part of the cost increase went to core businesses and vehicle finance, and scale-up timing is one to two years out.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Middle East conflict on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a drag on growth, not a decline; inventory moved through March but April-May saw some drag on intercity truck activity.

qa_highlights.question: Do growth businesses have contribution-level profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all businesses are contribution-margin positive; negative numbers arise only at EBITDA level or below.

OMC fuel loyalty programme suspension affecting fuel business revenue.
Margin pressure from growth business investment; adjusted EBITDA margin trended from ~36% in Q1 FY26 to ~31%.

Vehicle finance is dependent on partner credit decisions; BlackBuck does not guarantee loan performance.
Senior team departures (three people in SMB/senior team per management) and competitive entry into the space.

544288|2026-06.headline: BlackBuck Q1 FY27: total income up ~38% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 16% to ₹55 crore, with reported PAT at ₹42 crore after a deferred-tax effect.
544288|2026-06.overview: Management said the business recovered through late May and June after a weak April caused by macro logistics headwinds. Revenue from operations grew ~42% YoY and ~10% QoQ, while net revenue grew 25% YoY and contribution margin held at ~93%. Adjusted EBITDA rose from ₹47 crore to ₹55 crore, and reported PAT of ₹42 crore fell sequentially from ₹66 crore because of a deferred tax item recognised in Q4 FY26. Growth businesses (Super Loads and vehicle finance) grew ~44% QoQ after ~20% QoQ last quarter.

segments.name: Core businesses (payments/tolling, telematics)
segments.commentary: Core revenue grew ~21% YoY and delivered a record quarter for profitability and cash flow. Telematics recorded its highest-ever quarterly new device sales, across AI, non-AI and specialised devices.

segments.name: Super Loads and vehicle finance (growth businesses)
segments.commentary: Growth businesses revenue is up ~2.5x YoY and grew ~44% QoQ, up from ~20% QoQ last quarter. Super Loads now operates in 14 cities. Vehicle finance is expected to reach profitability by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tolling demand has normalised after April; management says it is back to its normal modelling framework (road growth, toll fare inflation, truck growth).
Fuel business is still uncertain. Management gave no timeline for full recovery in fuel loyalty margins.
Super Loads will keep investing aggressively; investment is stepping up each quarter.
Vehicle finance expected to converge to profitability by end of FY27 (reaffirmed).
Effective tax: for the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax; the loss-utilisation view will be reassessed in Q4.
Super Loads segment-level disclosure expected in about three to four quarters, once the business is large enough.
capex_capacity: Super Loads present in 14 cities (4 initial cities plus 10 launched by March/April 2026); live in under 5% of India's industrial hubs.

First Super Loads hub is close to the ~250 loads/day (about 5,000/month) milestone; management says it is about 60-70% there on playbook building, and 70-80% of newer cities are growing faster than the first four.
Telematics device depreciation is front-loaded over two years, which raised depreciation this quarter.
About 40-50% of Super Loads loads are AI-enabled on a given day.
demand_pricing: Tolling GTV grew 16% YoY, which management says is only a low single-digit rise at NETC level and a higher single-digit rise against the CV market.

Renewal rates for telematics: first renewal around 80% for GPS products (early 70s by some accounts), stabilising in the 80s for second and third renewals; higher-end products run 5-10 percentage points better.
Fuelling is a small share of revenue. Management said loyalty margin spend is discretionary and fuel recovery is only partial.
On Delhivery's possible entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance, management sees it as positive for the industry and does not expect near-term threat.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra (Axis Capital): Which hubs is Super Loads present in, daily load volumes, and outlook for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Present in 14 cities; the first four are Bangalore, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Chennai. Super Loads sequential growth was ~50%, up from ~23-24% a quarter earlier. Detailed volume disclosure is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse (JM Financial): Will the macro headwinds in tolling and fuelling taper in Q2 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolling caution has gone away and BAU is restored after a sharp April contraction in normalised swipe metrics. Fuel is only partially recovered, and management gave no timeline for a full recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse: Is Delhivery's entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance a medium-term threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees it as a positive for the industry since there is little qualified competition. It sees no near-term threat and will watch market share closely.

qa_highlights.question: Abhisek Banerjee (ICICI Securities): What drives the 13% growth in transacting users, and what share of users use Super Loads?
qa_highlights.answer: User growth is driven by tolling, telematics and marketplace acquisition, which have been secular for 10-12 quarters. Super Loads is a low-frequency use case and too early to move usage minutes (under 5% of hubs covered).

qa_highlights.question: Monica Joshi: What learnings from earlier cities are being applied to new ones, and how are Bangalore like-for-like numbers trending?
qa_highlights.answer: New cities are layered and run with several parallel experiments; AI-first, less people-dependent workflows are used. Management declined to give like-for-like Bangalore numbers until the segment is large enough to report separately.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra: What is the effective tax rate this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: For the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax. The loss-utilisation position will be reassessed at the end of the year (Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Lokesh Manik (Vallum Capital): Why did depreciation rise, and why did GTV fall from ₹6,800 crore to ₹6,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Telematics devices are depreciated over two years, so depreciation is front-loaded with the device investment. GTV now reports tolling only, with fuelling removed because of fuel price uncertainty.

risks_watch: Fuel business recovery: no timeline given, and fuel loyalty spend is discretionary.
Tolling volume: tolling transactions fell 3% QoQ, and tolling GTV growth (16%) lags NETC and the CV market.
Super Loads investment: spending rises each quarter, and segment-level disclosure is not expected for 3-4 quarters.
Reported PAT volatility from deferred tax; the Q4 loss-utilisation reassessment could move reported earnings.
Potential competition from Delhivery in tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance.

544290|2026-03.headline: Enviro Infra FY26 revenue rose 7.5% to INR11,456 mn, missing 35% guidance; FY27 guided to ~INR2,000 crore revenue with 13.5-14% PAT margin.
544290|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR4,273 mn (+8.8% YoY), EBITDA INR799 mn (18.7% margin) and PAT INR543 mn (12.4% margin), with margin pressure attributed to renewable IPP mix, higher employee cost, ECL provision and depreciation. Management said FY26 revenue partly missed guidance because awarded projects stayed in design and bid evaluations were delayed, and it cut FY27 EBITDA guidance to 21-22% from 22-24% citing commodity cost pressure. Working capital stretched to 166 days (unbilled revenue days at 195) because AMRUT state-scheme funds were delayed. The renewable segment (BESS, wind EPC via Suyog Urja) is now a major part of the order book.

financial_highlights.value: INR422 crore (LT INR250 crore, ST INR175 crore)

segments.name: Water & wastewater
segments.commentary: Execution order book about INR2,733 crore plus O&M order book about INR951 crore; FY27 water/wastewater revenue expected about INR1,350 crore. Recent wins: INR348 crore BUIDCO (Bihar) project and two Swachh Bharat sanitation projects in Pune and Nashik worth INR824 crore in Q4.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Execution order book about INR2,051 crore plus O&M/IPP about INR1,079 crore; renewable revenue was about INR129 crore in FY26 (INR117 crore in Q4, mostly IPP with near-zero margin). FY27 renewable revenue target about INR650 crore; BESS EPC PAT margin guided about 10%, renewables blended PAT 10-12%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR2,000 crore, with PAT of INR270-280 crore (13.5-14% PAT margin).
FY27 EBITDA margin cut to 21-22% from earlier 22-24%, with a possible further 1-2 percentage point dip from commodity and geopolitical cost pressure.
FY27 order inflow target of at least INR2,500 crore; bid pipeline submitted about INR1,200 crore plus about INR5,000 crore under evaluation.
Working capital cycle targeted to fall to about 90 days; debt-to-equity to be capped at 1:1 on consolidated basis.
Capex for FY27 expected at about INR20-30 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue said to be well above Q1 FY26 (about INR250 crore), without a number.
FY28 indicative revenue from existing order book about INR2,500-2,800 crore; management reiterated 35-40% long-term topline growth ambition.
capex_capacity: Total execution order book about INR4,800 crore, said to give visibility over FY27 and FY28 (execution period 18-24 months for renewable projects).
BESS: 4 NTPC EPC projects totalling 930 MWh worth about INR1,070 crore (UP, Assam, Karnataka, Telangana) plus acquired 150 MWh Bihar BESS project.
Lithium-ion cell procurement deferred due to price rises; BOS works (civil, transformers, HT lines) already started.
Renewable team above 250 professionals; business heads appointed for each division.
Asset monetisation possible if leverage rises; Suyog Urja (wind EPC) acquired during FY26.
demand_pricing: Most contracts carry a price variation clause, which offsets only part of the cost increase; management says guidance was lowered for this gap.
Water project cost benchmarks: STP INR1-1.5 crore per MLD; water treatment INR30-50 lakh per MLD; CETP highly variable (INR2-15 crore per MLD).
Design component is 2-5% of turnkey water project value; STPs and CETPs are the most technology-intensive.

Revenue shortfall attributed to slow evaluations and re-bidding of an MIDC CETP/ZLD project and two Bangalore projects stuck in design, plus delayed AMRUT funds in Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab.
Renewable receivables de-risked via NTPC and A-to-AAA rated private clients for Suyog's wind EPC work.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue guidance (about 35% growth) missed and is execution delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ongoing projects have no delays, but the order book of about INR1,200 crore at 1 April 2025 converted to about INR1,145 crore (about 95%) with timing slipping; some projects stayed in design and a re-bid hit timelines. Renewables were about INR100 crore below the INR200 crore guidance and wastewater about INR100 crore below as well.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what is the underlying margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited mix: about INR100-120 crore of zero-margin IPP revenue, employee cost up to about 6% of revenue, other expenses 3.5%, ECL provision INR10 crore and depreciation up about INR25 crore. Manufacturing cost fell about 1 percentage point; FY26 EBITDA stayed above 24%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of renewable revenue in FY26 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable revenue was about INR129 crore for FY26, with about INR12 crore up to December and INR117 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital cycle was 166 days, with UBR days at 195 because AMRUT funds were not released; receivable days fell to 53. Management expects funds from Chhattisgarh and a path for Rajasthan, Haryana and MP, targeting about 90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA guidance be cut further and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cut EBITDA guidance to 21-22% from 22-24% due to commodity and geopolitical cost pressure; a further 1-2 point dip is possible, depending on whether the situation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS and renewable margins and how is the FY27 revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS EPC PAT margin is about 10%; renewable blended PAT target is 10-12%. FY27 revenue split is about INR1,350 crore water/wastewater and INR650 crore renewables, against the INR2,000 crore total; about 42% of the INR4,800 crore order book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow position?
qa_highlights.answer: Adjusted pre-tax OCF is roughly balanced (about INR4 lakh positive) in FY26; post-tax OCF is negative INR63 crore, mainly due to service concession receivables recognised in OCF under audit policy.

risks_watch: Delayed central and state fund release (AMRUT, Jal Jeevan) could keep UBR days near 195 and working capital above 166 days.
Lithium-ion cell cost increases and geopolitical commodity pressure could cut EBITDA by a further 1-2 percentage points.
Revenue execution slippage: FY26 missed guidance; FY27 guidance of about INR2,000 crore depends on converting only about 42% of the INR4,800 crore order book.
Renewable IPP projects carry near-zero margin; segment profitability disclosure is promised separately going forward.
Debt rising toward the stated 1:1 debt-to-equity ceiling as renewable development projects are funded.

544290|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR359.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 21.07% from 26.65%, and FY27 guidance was trimmed to 21-22%.
544290|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR359.2 crore (+49% YoY) with EBITDA of INR75.7 crore (+17.9% YoY) and PAT of INR45.2 crore (+6.5% YoY). Management attributed the margin compression to higher raw material costs, a renewables mix, and a step-up in employee cost (about 7% of revenue vs 3-3.5% earlier). Total order book is about INR6,721 crore, split INR3,694 crore water/wastewater and INR3,027 crore renewables and BESS. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,000 crore and PAT of INR260-270 crore, while lowering the EBITDA margin guidance to 21-22% from 22-24%, and later described a blended 19-20% margin.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the gross margin decline YoY, and was it raw material costs or industry competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher raw material costs, the renewables mix, and employee cost rising to about 7% of Q1 revenue from 3-3.5% earlier (team grew from about 900 at IPO to about 2,300); employee cost to normalise to 5-5.5% and finance cost to 3-3.5% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timelines for the order book and O&M duration?
qa_highlights.answer: Water execution INR2,700 crore over 18-24 months; renewables INR2,000 crore over 12-18 months; water O&M 5-15 years (about 10 years average), renewable O&M 5-12 years for EPC and 25 years for IPP.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify raw material impact and segment EBITDA margins; any price pass-through on new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Water 21-22%, renewables 15-18%, blended 19-20%, around 20% for the year. Raw material impact about 1-2% of topline; WPI/CPI-linked price variation covers part, with some increase absorbed in EPC pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Wind revenue contribution and renewable EPC vs O&M split?
qa_highlights.answer: Wind (Suyog Urja) contributed INR80 crore of INR359 crore Q1 revenue; renewable execution order book about INR2,000 crore and O&M/IPP about INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Peak debt, bidding pipeline and exit FY27 order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renewables saw no margin downside; pipeline of about INR3,000 crore under evaluation plus INR6,000-7,000 crore being bid; renewables not being pushed aggressively; wind EPC INR600-800 crore targeted. No peak debt figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue and working capital status; will operating cash flow turn positive in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital described as still bloated and funds flow slow, with management expecting a healthier cash flow position when cash flow numbers come out in September. Service concession receivables take about INR85 crore out of OCF; OCF turning positive is hoped for but not guaranteed. JJM exposure about INR150-160 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Suyog Urja tranche payments and FY27 revenue and profit contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition valued INR311 crore: INR111 crore paid, INR100 crore second tranche after FY27 (around July) subject to KPIs, third tranche after FY28. Suyog FY27 revenue expectation INR400-450 crore at 15-16% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue (about INR360 crore) below the run-rate implied by historical seasonality, and is the INR2,000 crore guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is on target as guided at about 20% of the year; a significant jump is expected from Q3 when NTPC BESS (930 MWh) procurement starts. Guidance of INR2,000 crore revenue and INR260-270 crore PAT reaffirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach INR2,500-3,000 crore, and what about desalination and overseas projects?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore is the threshold guidance, with about 50% conversion of the INR2,700 crore water execution book implying INR1,300-1,350 crore. Overseas bids submitted; desalination projects being pursued; operations in 17 states; ZLD and CBG projects under way.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook beyond FY27 and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a bare-minimum growth target of 25-30% a year while maintaining healthy margins, and said it will avoid low-margin projects. Margin upside possible but guidance based on minimum levels.

544291|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 52% to ₹1,628 Cr with PAT of ₹143 Cr (8.8% margin); order book stands at ₹3,326 Cr with ₹2,200 Cr of bids pending results.
544291|2026-03.overview: Rajesh Power reported FY26 revenue of ₹1,628 Cr (+52% YoY), EBITDA of ₹197 Cr (+59%, 12.1% margin) and PAT of ₹143 Cr (+48%, 8.8% margin). H2 FY26 revenue rose 30% YoY to ₹990 Cr, but H2 EBITDA margin (11.4%) and PAT margin (8.5%) were lower than full-year levels, which management attributed to billing mix. Order inflow for FY26 was ₹2,743 Cr and the unexecuted order book closed at ₹3,326 Cr, below the ~₹4,500 Cr previously flagged, which management blamed on delayed tender results. Receivables rose sharply to ~₹350 Cr, which management attributed to heavy March billing, and payables rose to about 58 days.

segments.name: Power distribution
segments.commentary: 71% of the ₹3,326 Cr order book (₹2,365 Cr). Management cites ~₹5,000 Cr addressable distribution opportunity in Gujarat, part of the robust infrastructure scheme. Competitors per bid: 4 to 6.

segments.name: Power transmission
segments.commentary: 29% of the order book (₹961 Cr). Pan-India push into Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Odisha, Jharkhand and Uttarakhand; Gujarat is 85-90% of the total order book. Competitors per bid: 3 to 4.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: Signed a 65 MW / 130 MWh standalone project for GUVNL on a build-own-operate, rental basis. Targeted IRR 10-12%; billing ~₹14-15 Cr per year; execution expected by September 2027, with Q1 FY27 mentioned as a possible earlier date.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of ~35-40% retained; management said 40% growth is planned for FY27 and roughly 40% CAGR over the next 3-4 years.
EBITDA margin guided at 11-12% and PAT margin at 8-9%, described as stabilised rather than rising.
FY26 order inflow target of ₹4,000-5,000 Cr targeted for the year ahead; closing order book target above ₹5,000 Cr for FY27.
Pending bids of ~₹2,200 Cr expected to conclude by end-May or first week of June 2026; combined bid book (~₹5,700-6,000 Cr) assumed at ~40% win rate.
Gujarat share of order book expected to move toward 80:20 (Gujarat:outside) in the near term from 85-90% today.
Working capital cycle of 30-40 days described as sustainable.
capex_capacity: BESS: capex estimated at ₹1.5-2.5 Cr per MW; project funded 70-80% by bank debt with the balance as equity (absolute equity amount not yet quantified).
BESS revenue: ₹1.89 lakh per MW, giving ~₹14-15 Cr annual billing on 65 MW.
First 400 kV GIS project for a private Gujarat client expected to commission in September-October 2026.
FY26 execution: 350+ feeders, 4,000+ ring main units, 1,200+ distribution transformers, 1,300+ km of cable laid; over 51,000 km of MVCC work under execution in Gujarat.
Projects are typically executed in 18-24 months; the company says upcoming mobilisation of a few projects is expected within the next 2 months.
demand_pricing: Addressable market claimed at ~₹14,000-15,000 Cr per year across Gujarat (GETCO ~₹4,000-4,500 Cr addressable from ~₹10,000 Cr annual capex; distribution ~₹5,000 Cr), Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Odisha, Jharkhand, and railway traction substations.
Price escalation clauses cover most items; management says raw material (aluminium, copper) increases are passed through back-to-back with no margin impact.
Cable-jointer attrition cited at 2-3%. Labour camps are placed near sites and management reports no LPG/West Asia-related labour shortage.
Insurance surety bonds now used in ~8-10% of non-Gujarat orders and expected to rise as more states include the clause in tenders.
Current L1 position: about ₹210 Cr of pre-tax value (H1 FY26 figure was ₹808 Cr).

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables (~₹350 Cr) and inventory jump versus H1 and last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a short-term effect from very high March billing, with no BESS receivables and no client payment delays; standard terms of 45-60 days stay. About ₹150 Cr had been collected from the ~₹348 Cr receivables by the call date. Debtor days are ~78 and are expected to return to ~60 as billing evens out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall short of the ~₹4,500 Cr target for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no shortfall in execution; the ~₹2,200 Cr of bids submitted in Q4 are still awaiting tender results, expected by end-May or early June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 gross and EBITDA margins decline, and what is the normal range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to billing mix. It sees project-level EBITDA of 11-12% and PAT of 8-9% as the normal range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall in H2 despite higher volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said corporate and project-management employee costs are not scaling with revenue. Its later figures showed employee cost rose from ₹43.9 Cr in FY25 to ₹59 Cr in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS economics (ownership, revenue, IRR, margin)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company will own and develop the 65 MW / 130 MWh asset, with monthly rental billing to GUVNL from around September 2027. Targeted IRR is 10-12%. Management said margins should match transmission, and that it is not bidding for more BESS projects, preferring BESS EPC.

qa_highlights.question: Is the working-capital stress visible in creditors, MSME dues and short-term borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no working-capital stress. Payables stretched to ~30-day credit terms from vendors, and MSME outstanding of ₹87 Cr was paid within 45 days except where agreed terms exceeded that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 400 kV GIS project and 765 kV expansion a margin opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 400 kV GIS project with a private Gujarat client is due for commissioning around September-October 2026. It described the margin commitment as stabilised at 11-12%, not expanding.

Conversion of the ~₹2,200 Cr pending bids by end-May or early June 2026, plus the ₹4,000-5,000 Cr FY27 inflow target.

544292|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% QoQ to INR4,282 million and EBITDA reached INR919 million, while management reiterated the FY28 target of US$400 million revenue at ~40% EBITDA margin.
544292|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery after a weak Q3, driven by the start of invoicing for drug-device combinations (DDC) and the India Semaglutide launch at the end of the quarter. Full-year revenue fell 2% YoY to INR14,216 million and EBITDA fell about 35%, both hit by delayed Semaglutide approvals. Management deferred the Steriscience injectables and Brooks merger scheme, citing smaller-investor valuation concerns and a lower listed-company share price, and said it will revisit in about two years. Capacity expansion remains on track, with a new DDC line expected to be available from next quarter and three lines installed by end FY27.

segments.name: DDC (drug-device combinations) / Semaglutide
segments.commentary: Invoicing began this year; Canada approvals received for two partners, and shipments to both Canadian partners have commenced. Current line is fully committed back-to-back, and the new 500-litre-capable line is expected to be available from next quarter.

segments.name: Injectables and soft gelatin (base business)
segments.commentary: Signed 10 new licences, launched 15-plus products and added customers during the year. Soft gelatin capacity is expected to be fully utilised within the current period, and a fourth injectable line is coming in unit two.

segments.name: Biologics (nascent)
segments.commentary: Funnel expanded almost 4x YoY; a European biosimilar partner, a US biosimilar major and a second animal-health project from a top-three global player were added. Management expects a meaningful contribution in FY28 and commercial manufacturing from FY29; no revenue or EBITDA split was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance reiterated: US$400 million organic revenue at around 40% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance not given beyond expecting a strong year and a sequential improvement in revenue and EBITDA each quarter.
Medium-term target of 50%-plus ROCE.

capex_capacity: Part of a US$100 million capex programme; the new line installed a couple of months ago is in qualification and expected to be available from Q1 FY27 (next quarter), with commercial availability in Q2.
Two additional lines are planned this year, giving three lines by end FY27; a fourth injectable line is coming in unit two.

Existing line capped at 200-litre batch size; new lines can go to 500 litres, and up to 750-1,000 litres in the longer term. Moving from 200 to 500 litres raises output about 2.5x (about 60,000 pens/day at 200 litres).
Sterile manufacturing capacity framed as about 225 sterile days per line, roughly 675 days across three lines.
Capacity expansion fully funded through incremental domestic and international bank borrowings; the company added about 400 people at its flagship site.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds supply for at least the next two years; customers have reserved capacity with upfront fees and take-or-pay contracts.
India Semaglutide: partners were present on day one across multiple brands, and the customer base holds almost two-thirds of the Indian generic market by value as of end April.
The company is first and only CDMO for the first three generic Semaglutide approvals in US and Canada; ANVISA approval received, positioning it for Brazil.
Brazil is said to be the largest market outside North America for Semaglutide; no Brazil market-size numbers were given. CDMO terms are ex-works, so tariffs fall on customers.
Oral Semaglutide seen as taking 25% to one-third of the market, with injectables remaining dominant.
Customer advances broadly unchanged from the INR250 crore reported last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil local-manufacturing duty risk and whether profit-share arrangements exist with other regulated-market customers.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 28% duty applies only where local manufacturing exists, which it does not yet in Brazil, and CDMO terms are ex-works. It declined to discuss customer-specific profit-share terms beyond what was public.

qa_highlights.question: Why inventories rose from INR158 crore (March 2025) to INR440 crore (March 2026) for a service provider.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inventory is customer-funded and fungible, pooled across customers, and is adjusted against customer advances with no material P&L risk; the P&L impact is limited to conversion fees.

qa_highlights.question: Why opex and staff costs rose despite lower revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is supporting the capacity expansion ahead of the second and third DDC lines, which underpins the FY28 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of DDC capacity and utilisation.
qa_highlights.answer: The new line is available from next quarter and will ease pressure on the existing line; three lines are expected by end FY27, and the sequential revenue and EBITDA improvement is tied to these additions.

qa_highlights.question: Biologics contribution timing and profitability.
qa_highlights.answer: Agreements are expected over FY27 and FY28, with a meaningful contribution in FY28 and commercial manufacturing from FY29. Management declined to give biologics revenue or EBITDA-loss figures.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year FY27 numbers and Canadian approvals for other clients.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated FY28 guidance only and gave no FY27 figures. It said more Canadian approvals are expected over the next few quarters but could not give a timeline.

Brazil and other emerging-market approvals, and the pace at which partners get them.

Working capital and inventory build (customer-funded), with normalisation expected in FY27.

544292|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR4,490 million and EBITDA to INR1,233 million (+39% YoY); FY28 guidance of $400M revenue and 40% margin reiterated.
544292|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR4,490 million grew 37% YoY, driven by the semaglutide commercial launch, new MSA contracts and new customer wins. EBITDA of INR1,233 million rose 39% YoY and 34% QoQ, with management attributing the margin step-up mainly to a higher drug-device combination (DDC) contribution. Management said capacity is full, with the second cartridge line commissioning this quarter and a third line due within FY27. FY28 guidance of $400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Each new line doubles sterile days

segments.name: Drug-device combination (DDC)
segments.commentary: Main driver of the margin improvement; second cartridge line commissioning this quarter, third line within FY27, and a fourth later in FY28. Management says existing cartridge capacity is fully utilised while pre-filled syringe capacity is largely available.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: Added Formycon (biosimilars) and an animal-health contract; RFP funnel is almost 4x what it was just over a year ago. Commercial revenue expected from FY29 onward, with mammalian and microbial capacity expansion under consideration.

segments.name: Soft gelatin
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded from 800 million to 2.4 billion units; the business is shifting from captive Strides IP to CDMO. Management expects the added capacity to be fully taken up over 12-15 months and has started a greenfield site process.

segments.name: Injectables (Steri-Science)
segments.commentary: Focused portfolio built around penicillin and FDA-shortage products. A sterile injectable site shutdown starts in Q2 and runs into Q3 to add pre-filled syringe and lyophilisation capacity.

Revenue and EBITDA expected to grow sequentially QoQ through FY27, with H2 weighted by new-line ramp-up and soft gel seasonality.
Opex already upfronted, so the full contribution from new lines is expected once all lines are in place.
Capex beyond the US$100 million programme for biologics expected to be significantly lower than DDC spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why has soft gel revenue not grown faster after capacity went from 800 million to 2.4 billion units?

qa_highlights.question: Did the injectable shutdown affect Q1, and what drove the sequential margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: The injectable shutdown starts this quarter and runs into Q2. The margin rise was attributed mainly to higher DDC contribution plus soft gel and injectable seasonality, which is H2-weighted.

qa_highlights.question: Is there order book visibility to achieve the $400 million FY28 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing DDC order book, biologics new contracts and funnel, soft gel customer additions and new injectable capabilities.

qa_highlights.question: Can the new lines be used for any customer, and will batch-size changes need regulatory approval?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across lines and customers; customers will be served from both lines. Batch size increases from 200 L to 500 L should be possible in most geographies with a quick approval, depending on the market.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q1 capture the full EBITDA contribution from line one?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue from line one reached full per-line contribution in Q1, but profitability will improve only once all lines are installed, because most opex has already been upfronted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook beyond the US$100 million programme?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of the US$100 million is committed. Biologics capacity expansion will need additional capex, expected to be significantly lower than DDC spend.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin outlook given the seasonal pattern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall EBITDA will not go below 34% for the year, with Q2 and Q4 strong and Q3 muted.

qa_highlights.question: Why has test volume growth slowed to about 10-11% from around 20% in prior quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was nothing specific and that the company would evaluate it; it did not give a reason.

qa_highlights.question: What is the genomics market size and B2B/B2C split?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is 80% B2C and 20% B2B, with B2B expected to grow as a share. Indian genomics market cited at about Rs 450 million by 2030 (figure as stated; unit unclear). Average realisation not given, since genomic test prices range from Rs 4,000-5,000 to over Rs 50,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROCE/ROE below national peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the young centre base (27 of 45 mature centres under 2 years old); lower only against three or four players.

qa_highlights.question: Are franchisee collection centres affected by new spokes?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; when a collection centre area proves strong, a spoke is opened and the franchisee is relocated to a further location.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance only 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: CSO said the company has been conservative as it is a relatively new organisation; no dearth of effort.

Revenue guidance of 15% for FY27 was described as conservative; watch whether actual growth exceeds it.
Capex of Rs 70-80 crore for FY27 and the 100-centre target by FY28 require sustained hub and spoke openings in new states such as Jharkhand, Assam and Tripura.

544294|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 62% YoY to about INR142 crores; FY26 revenue up 87% to INR485 crores, but margins fell and management guided to similar growth in FY27.

Margins were lower than previously guided, which management attributed to qualification and investment costs for new semiconductor and space customers. Management guided to similar growth in FY27 and said margins would improve, and it is pursuing a QIP sized at about 7-10% of market cap.

segments.commentary: Landmark multi-year space contract of about INR400 crores won in FY26; first large production batches executed. Management expects 300-400% growth in FY27, with the customer base being expanded, including Amazon as the current customer.

Management said semiconductor could reach US$200 million revenue in 3-5 years.

Boeing agreed to level-load future schedules.

qa_highlights.question: Will the QIP be used to reduce debt, and how will working capital be managed?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Boeing T-7 contract and when will it ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategic agreements of about USD 200 million are in place and orders have been received. Zeena Philip said the ramp-up would begin later in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the PAT margin and cash flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said cash flow should improve in coming years. The MD said PAT margin depends on QIP timing, and PAT is expected to improve in FY27 if current trends continue.

qa_highlights.answer: About 20% of FY26 revenue came from semiconductor and space; management said their margins are in the 17-22% range.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it uses back-to-back supplier contracts and escalation clauses, with some customers accepting EPA clauses and others not.

544296|2026-03.headline: Nisus standalone core revenue rose 110% YoY to INR 141 crore and PAT to INR 68 crore (48% margin) in FY26, with Q4 PAT of INR 11 crore.
544296|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year as a listed company, and management said core standalone revenue (ex-NCCCL) of INR 141 crore beat the INR 120-140 crore guidance despite a Q4 slowdown tied to West Asia conflict. Q4 core PAT was INR 11 crore, and the consolidated group (including NCCCL, acquired August 2025) reported revenue of INR 575 crore and PAT of INR 83 crore. Management said UAE transactions worth over INR 500 crore were deferred rather than lost, and FY27 guidance is presented as a two-scenario framework rather than a point estimate. NCCCL's PAT rose to INR 16.4 crore from INR 3.5 crore, and its order book was INR 1,833 crore at March-end, plus INR 870 crore added in April-May 2026.

segments.name: Fund and asset management (core)
segments.commentary: Management said fund and asset management is now about 55% of core revenue versus advisory at about 45%; fee income is largely from sponsor capital in own funds plus treasury/investment income. UAE GCC portfolio of four assets reported 30% NAV growth in latest valuation, with management saying no impairment.

segments.name: Transaction advisory (core)
segments.commentary: Advisory held firm in Q4 despite the UAE transaction slowdown and was described as the counter-cyclical offset; advisory share was 67% of revenue when the business started versus about 55% now.

FY27 revenue-to-AUM ratio assumed at around 2.85% (blended), with management calling 3% a steady-state assumption versus 5.3-5.6% in FY26, which included one-off UAE advisory contracts and book investment gains.
NCCCL FY27 target of about INR 850 crore revenue; management aims for 3-4x turnover over the next year per Vice Chairman, with EBITDA margins of 9-10%.
REIC Ops fund (launched 2019) expected to wind up in 2026, with management fee booking expected more likely in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline: India about INR 700 crore (60-70% at term sheet); UAE about INR 2,000 crore being renegotiated on entry prices; management expects India deployment over the next couple of quarters.

Two India transactions (about INR 150 crore each) slipped by a few months due to Pune land demarcation methodology change, lender committee NOC delays, and RERA/e-Khata issues in Gujarat, Karnataka and Telangana; management expects these to close in the current quarter.
UAE deferred deals: one INR 500 crore transaction and one INR 300 crore transaction pushed to later closure.
NCCCL migrating to SAP HANA and adopting digital project management tools.
demand_pricing: Dubai: off-plan share fell from about 78% last year to much smaller levels as ready-to-move-in inventory rose to about 60-70%; investor purchases fell from about 87% (2017-18) to about 45%, with end-users at about 55%.

Management said it is buying at discounts to market and that renegotiation of entry prices is underway on the INR 2,000 crore UAE pipeline.
NCCCL works on 3-4 year order book visibility; industry EBITDA norm 9-10%, PAT 3-4%.
Management said advisory fees are directly correlated with AUM and fund size, and that the blended AUM-fee mix should shift toward management fees over time.

qa_highlights.answer: Avadhoot Sarwate said Pune demarcation methodology changed, and consortium lender NOCs took longer (March to May); about two trades of roughly INR 150 crore each slipped by a few months and are expected this quarter. qa_highlights.answer: Aanchal Singh said SEBI approval for the Neon Fund came the previous day, with launch from Q2; INR 1,800 crore fund plus INR 500 crore green shoe, fees broadly INR 220 crore, 7.5-year tenure. REIC Ops has a 12% hurdle with no catch-up, closing this year, with fees more likely in Q2.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the segment reporting does not split recurring fees from treasury income; fee income is described as small relative to the fund and asset management segment, which includes treasury income from sponsor capital in own funds. No quantified run-rate was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue-to-AUM assumed at 2.85% versus 5.3% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was inflated by high-margin UAE advisory contracts and book investment gains on yield compression; 3% is the steady-state assumption, and capital is expected to deploy mainly in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the India (INR 700 crore) and UAE (INR 2,000 crore) pipelines?

Tokenisation and Neon fund launches depend on regulatory approvals (token licence and white paper; SEBI approved Neon fund).
